translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 102.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 102.

sentences.zh: 【晉紀二十四】 起屠維大荒落，盡上章敦牂，凡二年。

translations.literal: Jin Annals 24: From Tuyang Dahuangluo through Shangzhang Dunzang; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Annals 24: From Tuyang Dahuangluo through Shangzhang Dunzang—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 海西公下太和四年（

translations.literal: Under the Deposed Emperor, fourth year of Taihe (
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor, fourth year of Taihe (

sentences.zh: 己巳，公元三六九年）

translations.literal: jisi, AD 369)
translations.idiomatic: jisi, AD 369)

sentences.zh: 春，三月，大司馬溫請與徐、兗二州刺史郗愔、江州刺史桓沖、豫州刺史袁真等伐燕。

translations.literal: In spring, the third month, Grand Marshal Huan Wen requested that he campaign against Yan together with Xi Yin, governor of Xu and Yan provinces, Huan Chong, governor of Jiang Province, Yuan Zhen, governor of Yu Province, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the third month, Grand Marshal Huan Wen asked to lead a campaign against Yan with Xi Yin, governor of Xu and Yan, Huan Chong of Jiang Province, Yuan Zhen of Yu Province, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 初，愔在北府，溫常雲：「京口酒可飲，兵可用。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yin was at the Northern Headquarters, Wen had often said, "The wine at Jingkou is drinkable, and the troops there are usable."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Xi Yin held the Northern Headquarters at Jingkou, Huan Wen had often remarked, "The wine at Jingkou is worth drinking, and the soldiers there are worth using."

sentences.zh: 深不欲愔居之；

translations.literal: He deeply did not want Yin to remain there;
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply unwilling to let Yin keep that post;

sentences.zh: 而愔暗於事機，乃遺溫箋，欲共獎王室，請督所部出河上。

translations.literal: yet Yin was dim about the situation and sent Wen a letter wishing to encourage the royal house together and asking to lead his command north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: but Yin failed to read the situation and sent Wen a letter offering to rally the royal house and asking to lead his forces north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 愔子超為溫參軍，取視，寸寸毀裂，乃更作愔箋，自陳非將帥才，不堪軍旅，老病，乞閒地自養，勸溫並領己所統。

translations.literal: Yin's son Chao was Wen's military aide; he took it to read, tore it inch by inch, then drafted another letter in Yin's name stating that he lacked the talent of a commander, could not bear military affairs, was old and ill, begged a quiet post to recuperate, and urged Wen to take over his command as well.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's son Xi Chao served as an aide on Wen's staff; he read the letter, tore it to shreds, and drafted a replacement in Yin's name declaring that he was no commander, unfit for the field, old and ill, and begging a quiet appointment to recover, while urging Wen to absorb his troops.

sentences.zh: 溫得箋大喜，即轉愔冠軍將軍、會稽內史，溫自領徐、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: Wen received the letter and was greatly pleased; he immediately transferred Yin to General Who Establishes Might and interior administrator of Kuaiji, while he himself took over the governorships of Xu and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was delighted by the letter and at once moved Yin to General Who Establishes Might and interior administrator of Kuaiji, while taking the Xu and Yan governorships for himself.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚戌，溫帥步騎五萬發姑孰。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on gengxu, Wen led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry forth from Gudu.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day gengxu, Wen marched from Gudu at the head of fifty thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 甲子，燕主暐立皇後可足渾氏，太后從弟尚書令豫章公翼之女也。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the Yan ruler Wei installed as empress Lady Kezuhun, daughter of Yizhang Duke Yi, younger cousin of the empress dowager and minister of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi, the Yan ruler Murong Wei made Lady Kezuhun his empress; she was the daughter of Yizhang Duke Murong Yi, the empress dowager's cousin and minister of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 大司馬溫自兗州伐燕。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Wen attacked Yan from Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Huan Wen advanced against Yan from Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 郗超曰：「道遠，汴水又淺，恐漕運難通。」

translations.literal: Xi Chao said, "The route is long, and the Bian River is again shallow; I fear grain transport by water will be hard to maintain."
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chao said, "The march is long, and the Bian is shallow again—we may not be able to keep the supply line open by water."

sentences.zh: 溫不從。

translations.literal: Wen did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Wen would not listen.

sentences.zh: 六月，辛丑，溫至金鄉，天旱，水道絕，溫使冠軍將軍毛虎生鑿巨野三百裡，引汶水會於清水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on xinchou, Wen reached Jinxiang; drought had cut off the waterways, so Wen had General Who Establishes Might Mao Husheng cut three hundred li through Juye to channel the Wen River into the Qing River.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinchou, Wen reached Jinxiang in a drought that had dried the waterways; he ordered General Who Establishes Might Mao Husheng to cut a three-hundred-li channel through Juye to bring the Wen River into the Qing.

sentences.zh: 虎生，寶之子也。

translations.literal: Husheng was the son of Mao Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Husheng was a son of Mao Bao.

sentences.zh: 溫引舟師自清水入河，舳艫數百裡。

translations.literal: Wen led his fleet from the Qing River into the Yellow River, the ships stretching for hundreds of li.
translations.idiomatic: Wen brought his fleet from the Qing into the Yellow River until the convoy stretched for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 郗超曰：「清水入河，難以通運。

translations.literal: Xi Chao said, "Once the Qing enters the Yellow River, transport will be hard to keep open.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chao said again, "Once the Qing joins the Yellow River, supplies will be hard to move.

sentences.zh: 若寇不戰，運道又絕，因敵為資，復無所得，此危道也。

translations.literal: If the enemy does not give battle and the transport route is again cut off, living off the enemy yet gaining nothing—this is a perilous course.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy refuses battle and the line is cut again, we would live off them yet take nothing—this is a dangerous path.

sentences.zh: 不若盡舉見眾直趨鄴城，彼畏公威名，必望風逃潰，北歸遼、碣。

translations.literal: Better to muster all the forces now visible and strike straight for Ye; they will fear your lordship's renown and surely flee at the sight of your banners north to Liao and Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Better to throw every man you have straight at Ye; they fear your name and will break and flee north to Liao and Jie.

sentences.zh: 若能出戰，則事可立決。

translations.literal: If they can be brought to battle, the affair can be settled at once.
translations.idiomatic: If they come out to fight, the matter can be decided quickly.

sentences.zh: 若欲城鄴而守之，則當此盛夏，難為功力。

translations.literal: If you wish to wall Ye and hold it, in this height of summer the labor will be hard to accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to fortify Ye and hold it, midsummer makes that work nearly impossible.

sentences.zh: 百姓布野，盡為官有，易水以南必交臂請命矣。

translations.literal: The common people are spread across the fields and would all become state property; south of the Yi River they would surely cross arms and submit.
translations.idiomatic: The people are scattered across the countryside and would all become yours; south of the Yi they would fold their arms and surrender.

sentences.zh: 但恐明公以此計輕銳，勝負難必，欲務持重，則莫若頓兵河、濟，控引漕運，俟資儲充備，至來夏乃進兵；

translations.literal: Yet I fear my lord may regard this plan as too light and swift, with victory uncertain; if you wish to be cautious, there is nothing better than halting the army on the Yellow and Ji, controlling grain transport, waiting until stores are full, and advancing only next summer;
translations.idiomatic: Yet you may think this plan too bold and the outcome uncertain; if you want caution, halt on the Yellow and Ji, secure the water route, fill the granaries, and march only next summer;

sentences.zh: 雖如賒遲，然期於成功而已。

translations.literal: though this seems slow, it aims only at success.
translations.idiomatic: slow as that seems, it is the way to succeed.

sentences.zh: 捨此二策而連軍北上，進不速決，退必愆乏。

translations.literal: If you abandon these two plans and march the army north in succession, advancing without a swift decision, retreat will surely bring want and shortage.
translations.idiomatic: If you reject both and push north in one long column, advance without a quick decision and retreat will mean want and exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 賊因此勢以日月相引，漸及秋冬，水更澀滯。

translations.literal: The enemy will use this situation to draw out day by day; as autumn and winter approach, the water will grow more sluggish.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy will drag things out day by day; by autumn and winter the rivers will run lower still.

sentences.zh: 且北土早寒，三軍裘褐者少，恐於時所憂，非獨無食而已。」

translations.literal: Moreover the north grows cold early; few in the three armies have fur and coarse cloth—what you should fear in season is not food alone."
translations.idiomatic: The north turns cold early, and few of the troops have winter gear—your seasonal worry will not be food alone."

sentences.zh: 溫又不從。

translations.literal: Wen again did not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Again Wen would not listen.

sentences.zh: 溫遣建威將軍檀玄攻湖陸，拔之，獲燕寧東將軍慕容忠。

translations.literal: Wen sent General Who Establishes Might Tan Xuan to attack Hulu, took it, and captured Yan's General Who Pacifies the East Murong Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wen sent General Who Establishes Might Tan Xuan against Hulu, captured the place, and took Yan's General Who Pacifies the East Murong Zhong.

sentences.zh: 燕主暐以下邳王厲為征討大都督，帥步騎二萬逆戰於黃墟，厲兵大敗，單馬奔還。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Wei appointed Prince of Xiapi Li grand commander for the punitive campaign and led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to meet the enemy at Huangxu; Li's army was utterly defeated and he fled back alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei made Prince of Xiapi Murong Li grand commander for the counterattack and led twenty thousand foot and horse to Huangxu; Li was routed and rode back alone.

sentences.zh: 高平太守徐翻舉郡來降。

translations.literal: Xu Fan, administrator of Gaoping, raised the whole commandery and came over.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fan, administrator of Gaoping, surrendered his entire commandery.

sentences.zh: 前鋒鄧遐、朱序敗燕將傅顏於林渚。

translations.literal: The vanguard Deng Xian and Zhu Xu defeated the Yan general Fu Yan at Linzhu.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard Deng Xian and Zhu Xu defeated Yan general Fu Yan at Linzhu.

sentences.zh: 暐復遣樂安王臧統諸軍拒溫，臧不能抗；

translations.literal: Wei again sent Prince of Le'an Zang to command the armies against Wen, but Zang could not resist;
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent Prince of Le'an Murong Zang to command the armies against Wen, but Zang could not hold;

sentences.zh: 乃遣散騎常侍李鳳求救於秦。

translations.literal: he then sent attendant cavalier Li Feng to beg aid from Qin.
translations.idiomatic: so he sent attendant cavalier Li Feng to seek aid from Former Qin.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，溫屯武陽，燕故兗州刺史孫元帥其族黨起兵應溫。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Wen encamped at Wuyang; Sun Yuan, former Yan governor of Yan Province, led his clan and followers to rise in support of Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Wen camped at Wuyang while Sun Yuan, Yan's former governor of Yan Province, rallied his kin to join Wen.

sentences.zh: 溫至枋頭，暐及太傅評大懼，謀奔和龍。

translations.literal: When Wen reached Fangtou, Wei and Grand Tutor Ping were greatly afraid and planned flight to Helong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen reached Fangtou, Wei and Grand Tutor Murong Ping were terrified and planned to flee to Helong.

sentences.zh: 吳王垂曰：「臣請擊之；

translations.literal: Prince of Wu Chui said, "Your servant asks to strike them;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wu Murong Chui said, "Let me attack them;

sentences.zh: 若其不捷，走未晚也。」

translations.literal: if we do not succeed, flight will not yet be late."
translations.idiomatic: if we fail, it will still be time to run."

sentences.zh: 暐乃以垂代樂安王臧為使持節、南討大都督，帥征南將軍范陽王德等眾五萬以拒溫。

translations.literal: Wei then replaced Prince of Le'an Zang with Chui as commissioner with full powers and grand commander for the southern campaign, leading General Who Campaigns South Prince of Fanyang De and fifty thousand men to resist Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Wei then replaced Murong Zang with Chui as commissioner with full powers and grand commander for the southern campaign, leading General Who Campaigns South Prince of Fanyang Murong De and fifty thousand men against Wen.

sentences.zh: 垂表司徒左長史申胤、黃門侍郎封孚、尚書郎悉羅騰皆從軍。

translations.literal: Chui memorialized that Chief Clerk of the Masters of Writing Shen Yin, Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Feng Fu, and Master of Writing Xiluo Teng should all accompany the army.
translations.idiomatic: Chui asked that chief clerk of the masters of writing Shen Yin, gentleman attendant at the yellow gate Feng Fu, and master of writing Xiluo Teng join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 胤，鐘之子；

translations.literal: Yin was the son of Zhong;
translations.idiomatic: Yin was a son of Shen Zhong;

sentences.zh: 孚，放之子也。

translations.literal: Fu was the son of Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was a son of Feng Fang.

sentences.zh: 暐又遣散騎侍郎樂嵩請救於秦，許賂以虎牢以西之地。

translations.literal: Wei again sent attendant cavalier Yue Song to beg rescue from Qin, promising as payment the lands west of Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei also sent attendant cavalier Yue Song to Qin for aid, offering all territory west of Hulao as payment.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅引群臣議於東堂，皆曰：「昔桓溫伐我，至灞上，燕不我救。

translations.literal: King of Qin Fu Jian gathered the ministers for discussion in the Eastern Hall; all said, "Formerly Huan Wen attacked us and reached Bashang, yet Yan did not rescue us.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian of Qin consulted his ministers in the Eastern Hall; all said, "When Huan Wen attacked us and reached Bashang, Yan did not help us.

sentences.zh: 今溫伐燕，我何救焉！

translations.literal: Now Wen attacks Yan—why should we rescue them!
translations.idiomatic: Now Wen attacks Yan—why should we save them!

sentences.zh: 且燕不稱籓於我，我何為救之！」

translations.literal: Moreover Yan does not call itself our vassal—why should we save them!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Yan does not acknowledge us as suzerain—why intervene!"

sentences.zh: 王猛密言於堅曰：「燕雖強大，慕容評非溫敵也。

translations.literal: Wang Meng spoke privately to Jian: "Though Yan is powerful, Murong Ping is no match for Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng told Jian privately, "Yan is strong, but Murong Ping cannot stand against Wen.

sentences.zh: 若溫舉山東，進屯洛邑，收幽、冀之兵，引並、豫之粟，觀兵崤、澠，則陛下大事去矣。

translations.literal: If Wen raises the Shandong region, advances to camp at Luoyang, gathers the armies of You and Ji, draws grain from Bing and Yu, and displays his forces at Xiao and Mian, then Your Majesty's great enterprise is lost.
translations.idiomatic: If Wen takes Shandong, camps at Luoyang, gathers the armies of You and Ji, draws grain from Bing and Yu, and threatens Xiao and Mian, your great enterprise is finished.

sentences.zh: 今不如與燕合兵以退溫；

translations.literal: Now it is better to join forces with Yan to drive Wen back;
translations.idiomatic: Better to join Yan now and drive Wen back;

sentences.zh: 溫退，燕亦病矣，然後我承其弊而取之，不亦善乎！」

translations.literal: when Wen retreats Yan will also be weakened; then we can take them at their exhaustion—is that not good!"
translations.idiomatic: when Wen withdraws Yan will be spent, and we can take them at their weakness—is that not wise!"

sentences.zh: 堅從之。

translations.literal: Jian followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Jian agreed.

sentences.zh: 八月，遣將軍苟池、洛州刺史鄧羌帥步騎二萬以救燕，出自洛陽，軍至穎川；

translations.literal: In the eighth month he sent General Gou Chi and Governor of Luo Province Deng Qiang leading twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to rescue Yan; they set out from Luoyang and the army reached Yingchuan;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he sent General Gou Chi and Luo governor Deng Qiang with twenty thousand foot and horse to aid Yan; they left Luoyang and reached Yingchuan;

sentences.zh: 又遣散騎侍郎姜撫報使於燕。

translations.literal: he also sent attendant cavalier Jiang Fu as envoy to report to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: and sent attendant cavalier Jiang Fu as envoy to Yan.

sentences.zh: 以王猛為尚書令。

translations.literal: Wang Meng was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 太子太傅封孚問於申胤曰：「溫眾強士整，乘流直進，今大軍徒逡巡高岸，兵不接刃，未見克殄之理，事將何如？」

translations.literal: Grand Tutor of the Heir Feng Fu asked Shen Yin: "Wen's masses are strong and his soldiers disciplined; riding the current he advances straight. Now our great army only loiters on the high banks without crossing blades—I see no way to destroy him. How will matters turn?"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor of the Heir Feng Fu asked Shen Yin, "Wen's host is strong and his troops in order; he drives upriver in a straight rush. Our army only prowls the high banks without closing—how can we destroy him? What will happen?"

sentences.zh: 胤曰：「以溫今日聲勢，似能有為。

translations.literal: Yin said, "By Wen's present fame and force he seems able to accomplish something.
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "By his present fame and force Wen looks capable.

sentences.zh: 然在吾觀之，必無成功。

translations.literal: Yet in my view he will certainly not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in my view he cannot succeed.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 晉室衰弱，溫專制其國，晉之朝臣未必皆與之同心。

translations.literal: The Jin house is weak; Wen monopolizes the state, and Jin courtiers are not necessarily all of one mind with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin house is weak and Wen dominates the state; the court is not necessarily united behind him.

sentences.zh: 故溫之得志，眾所不願也，必將乖阻以敗其事。

translations.literal: Therefore Wen's success is what many do not wish; they will surely obstruct him and ruin his affair.
translations.idiomatic: His success is what many do not want; they will work against him and ruin the campaign.

sentences.zh: 又，溫驕而恃眾，怯於應變。

translations.literal: Moreover Wen is arrogant and trusts his numbers, timid in adapting to change.
translations.idiomatic: He is arrogant, overconfident in numbers, and slow to adapt.

sentences.zh: 大眾深入，值可乘之會，反更逍遙中流，不出赴利，欲望持久，坐取全勝；

translations.literal: His great host has penetrated deep; when a chance to strike was at hand he instead drifted midstream, not going out for advantage, hoping to endure and win a complete victory by sitting still;
translations.idiomatic: His army is deep in enemy country; when a chance came he lingered on the river instead of striking, hoping to wait out a complete victory;

sentences.zh: 若糧廩愆懸，情見勢屈，必不戰自敗，此自然之數也。」

translations.literal: if granaries run short and his plight shows his strength bent, he will surely be defeated without fighting—this is the natural course."
translations.idiomatic: when the granaries fail and his plight shows, he will collapse without a battle—that is how these things go."

sentences.zh: 溫以燕降人段思為鄉導，悉羅騰與溫戰，生擒思。

translations.literal: Wen used the Yan surrenderer Duan Si as guide; Xiluo Teng fought Wen and captured Si alive.
translations.idiomatic: Wen used the Yan defector Duan Si as guide; Xiluo Teng fought him and took Si alive.

sentences.zh: 溫使故趙將李述徇趙、魏，騰又與虎賁中郎將染干津擊斬之，溫軍奪氣。

translations.literal: Wen sent the former Zhao general Li Shu to range through Zhao and Wei; Teng again joined Tiger Guard Central Commander Ranggan Jin to strike and kill him, and Wen's army lost its spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Wen sent the former Zhao general Li Shu to sweep Zhao and Wei; Teng and Tiger Guard central commander Ranggan Jin killed him, and Wen's army lost heart.

sentences.zh: 初，溫使豫州刺史袁真攻譙、梁，開石門以通水運，真克譙、梁而不能開石門，水運路塞。

translations.literal: Earlier Wen had sent Governor of Yu Province Yuan Zhen to attack Qiao and Liang and open Shimen to clear the water route; Zhen took Qiao and Liang but could not open Shimen, and the water transport route was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wen had sent Yu governor Yuan Zhen to take Qiao and Liang and open Shimen for the water route; Zhen captured both towns but failed to open Shimen, and the supply line by water was cut.

sentences.zh: 九月，燕范陽王德帥騎一萬、蘭台治書侍御史劉當帥騎五千屯石門，豫州刺史李邽帥州兵五千斷溫糧道。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Yan's Prince of Fanyang De led ten thousand horse, and Supervising Secretary of the Orchid Terrace Liu Dang led five thousand horse to camp at Shimen; Governor of Yu Province Li Gui led five thousand provincial troops to cut Wen's grain route.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Prince of Fanyang Murong De led ten thousand horse and Orchid Terrace supervising secretary Liu Dang five thousand horse to hold Shimen, while Yu governor Li Gui led five thousand provincial troops to sever Wen's supply line.

sentences.zh: 當，佩之子也。

translations.literal: Dang was the son of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Dang was a son of Liu Pei.

sentences.zh: 德使將軍慕容宙帥騎一千為前鋒，與晉兵遇。

translations.literal: De sent General Murong Zhou with one thousand horse as vanguard; they met Jin troops.
translations.idiomatic: De sent General Murong Zhou with a thousand horse as vanguard; they met Jin forces.

sentences.zh: 宙曰：「晉人輕剽，怯於陷敵，勇於乘退，宜設餌以釣之。」

translations.literal: Zhou said, "Jin men are light and swift, timid about closing with the enemy but bold in pursuing a retreat—we should set bait to hook them."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou said, "Jin troops are rash—shy of a hard fight but eager to chase a retreat. We should bait them."

sentences.zh: 乃使二百騎挑戰，分餘騎為三伏。

translations.literal: He then sent two hundred horse to challenge and divided the rest into three ambushes.
translations.idiomatic: He sent two hundred horse to provoke them and hid the rest in three ambushes.

sentences.zh: 挑戰者兵未交而走，晉兵追之；

translations.literal: The challengers fled before blades met, and Jin troops pursued;
translations.idiomatic: The challengers feigned flight before contact, and the Jin troops pursued;

sentences.zh: 宙帥伏以擊之，晉兵死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Zhou led the ambush to strike them, and very many Jin soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou sprang the ambush and killed a great many Jin soldiers.

sentences.zh: 溫戰數不利，糧儲復竭，又聞秦兵將至，丙申，焚舟，棄輜重、鎧仗，自陸道奔還。

translations.literal: Wen fought several times without advantage; stores were again exhausted, and he heard Qin troops were coming; on bingshen he burned the ships, abandoned baggage, armor, and weapons, and fled back by land.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated defeats and empty stores, with Qin troops reported on the way, on bingshen Wen burned his fleet, abandoned baggage and arms, and fled overland.

sentences.zh: 以毛虎生督東燕等四郡諸軍事，領東燕太守。

translations.literal: Mao Husheng was made supervisor of military affairs for Dongyan and three other commanderies and concurrently administrator of Dongyan.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Husheng was left to supervise military affairs in Dongyan and three other commanderies as administrator of Dongyan.

sentences.zh: 溫自東燕出倉垣，鑿井而飲，行七百餘里。

translations.literal: Wen left Dongyan for Cangyuan, dug wells to drink, and marched more than seven hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Wen marched from Dongyan toward Cangyuan, digging wells as he went, covering more than seven hundred li.

sentences.zh: 燕之諸將爭欲追之，吳王垂曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Yan's generals all wanted to pursue; Prince of Wu Chui said, "You must not.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's generals clamored to pursue; Prince of Wu Chui said, "No.

sentences.zh: 溫初退惶恐，必嚴設警備，簡精銳為後拒，擊之未必得志，不如緩之。

translations.literal: Wen has just retreated in fear and will surely set strict guards and pick elite troops as rearguard; to strike may not succeed—better to hold back.
translations.idiomatic: He has just retreated in panic and will post tight guards and elite rearguards; a strike may fail—better wait.

sentences.zh: 彼幸吾未至，必晝夜疾趨；

translations.literal: Thinking us not yet arrived, they will surely hurry day and night;
translations.idiomatic: Thinking us far behind, they will march day and night;

sentences.zh: 俟其士眾力盡氣衰，然後擊之，無不克矣。」

translations.literal: wait until their soldiers' strength is spent and their spirit faded, then strike—there is none you cannot overcome."
translations.idiomatic: when their men are spent and their spirit gone, strike—then you cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 乃帥八千騎徐行躡其後。

translations.literal: He then led eight thousand horse at an easy pace to follow their trail.
translations.idiomatic: He led eight thousand horse at an easy pace in their wake.

sentences.zh: 溫果兼道而進。

translations.literal: Wen indeed marched by double stages.
translations.idiomatic: Wen did march by forced stages.

sentences.zh: 數日，垂告諸將曰：「溫可擊矣。」

translations.literal: After several days Chui told the generals, "Wen can be struck now."
translations.idiomatic: After several days Chui told his officers, "Wen is ready to be hit."

sentences.zh: 乃急追之，及溫於襄邑。

translations.literal: He then pressed the pursuit and caught Wen at Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the pursuit and caught Wen at Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 范陽王德先帥勁騎四千伏於襄邑東澗中，與垂夾擊溫，又破之，死者復以萬計。

translations.literal: Prince of Fanyang De had first led four thousand crack horse in ambush in the eastern ravine at Xiangyi; with Chui he struck Wen from both sides and defeated him again, the dead again numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Fanyang De had hidden four thousand elite horse in the eastern ravine at Xiangyi; with Chui he caught Wen in a pincer and routed him again, with tens of thousands more dead.

sentences.zh: 孫元遂據武陽以拒燕，燕左衛將軍孟高討擒之。

translations.literal: Sun Yuan then held Wuyang to resist Yan; Yan's Left Guard General Meng Gao attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuan held Wuyang against Yan; Yan's Left Guard General Meng Gao captured him.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己巳，大司馬溫收散卒，屯於山陽。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jisi, Grand Marshal Wen gathered scattered troops and encamped at Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jisi, Grand Marshal Wen rallied his scattered troops and camped at Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 溫深恥喪敗，乃歸罪於袁真，奏免真為庶人；

translations.literal: Wen was deeply shamed by the defeat and shifted blame to Yuan Zhen, memorializing to strip Zhen to commoner status;
translations.idiomatic: Deeply shamed by the defeat, Wen blamed Yuan Zhen and memorialized to reduce him to commoner status;

sentences.zh: 又免冠軍將軍鄧遐官。

translations.literal: he also removed General of the Gentlemen of the Household Deng Xian from office.
translations.idiomatic: he also stripped General of the Gentlemen of the Household Deng Xian of his post.

sentences.zh: 真以溫誣己，不服，表溫罪狀，朝廷不報。

translations.literal: Zhen, holding that Wen had slandered him, would not submit and memorialized Wen's offenses; the court gave no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, believing Wen had framed him, refused to submit and memorialized Wen's crimes; the court did not respond.

sentences.zh: 真遂據壽春叛，降燕，且請救；

translations.literal: Zhen then held Shouchun in rebellion, submitted to Yan, and also begged rescue;
translations.idiomatic: Zhen then seized Shouchun and rebelled, submitted to Yan, and asked for aid;

sentences.zh: 亦遣使如秦。

translations.literal: he also sent envoys to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: he also sent envoys to Qin.

sentences.zh: 溫以毛虎生領淮南太守，守歷陽。

translations.literal: Wen had Mao Husheng take charge as administrator of Huainan and guard Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wen put Mao Husheng in charge as administrator of Huainan to hold Liyang.

sentences.zh: 燕、秦既結好，使者數往來。

translations.literal: Yan and Qin having made alliance, envoys went back and forth repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yan and Qin were allied, envoys traveled between them constantly.

sentences.zh: 燕散騎侍郎太原郝晷、給事黃門侍郎梁琛相繼如秦。

translations.literal: Yan's attendant cavalier Hao Zhao of Taiyuan and gentleman attendant at the yellow gate Liang Chen went to Qin in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's attendant cavalier Hao Zhao of Taiyuan and gentleman attendant at the yellow gate Liang Chen went to Qin in turn.

sentences.zh: 晷與王猛有舊，猛接以平生，問晷東方之事。

translations.literal: Zhao was old friends with Wang Meng; Meng received him as in former days and asked Zhao about affairs in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was an old acquaintance of Wang Meng, who received him warmly and asked about conditions in the east.

sentences.zh: 晷見燕政不修而秦大治，知燕將亡，陰欲自托於猛，頗洩其實。

translations.literal: Zhao saw Yan's government neglected while Qin was well governed, knew Yan would perish, secretly wished to entrust himself to Meng, and largely revealed the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Yan's government in decay and Qin thriving, Zhao knew Yan would fall and quietly sought Meng's protection, letting much of the truth slip.

sentences.zh: 琛至長安，秦王堅方畋於萬年，欲引見琛，琛曰：「秦使至燕，燕之君臣朝服備禮，灑掃宮庭，然後敢見。

translations.literal: When Chen reached Chang'an, King of Qin Fu Jian was hunting at Wannian and wished to summon him for audience; Chen said, "When a Qin envoy comes to Yan, Yan's ruler and ministers don court dress and full ritual, sweep the palace courtyard, and only then dare receive him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen reached Chang'an, King Fu Jian was hunting at Wannian and wished to receive him at once; Chen said, "When a Qin envoy comes to Yan, our ruler and ministers dress in full court regalia, sweep the palace court, and only then receive him.

sentences.zh: 今秦王欲野見之，使臣不敢聞命！」

translations.literal: Now the King of Qin wishes to receive me in the wild—your servant dares not accept such a command!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the King of Qin wishes to meet me in the open field—I cannot accept such a command!"

sentences.zh: 尚書郎辛勁謂琛曰：「賓客入境，惟主人所以處之，君焉得專制其禮！

translations.literal: Master of Writing Xin Jin said to Chen, "When a guest enters a state, only the host decides how to receive him—how can you monopolize the ritual!
translations.idiomatic: Master of writing Xin Jin said to Chen, "When a guest enters a country, the host decides the reception—how can you dictate the ritual!

sentences.zh: 且天子稱乘輿，所至曰行在所，何堂居之有！

translations.literal: Moreover the Son of Heaven is called 'imperial carriage'; wherever he stops is called 'where the procession halts'—what fixed hall could there be!
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven travels in the imperial carriage; wherever he stops is the 'traveling palace'—what fixed hall is there!

sentences.zh: 又，《春秋》亦有遇禮，何為不可乎！」

translations.literal: Besides, the Spring and Autumn Annals also records the rite of encounter—why may it not be done!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the Spring and Autumn Annals records the rite of encounter—why not!"

sentences.zh: 琛曰：「晉室不綱，靈祚歸德，二方承運，俱受明命。

translations.literal: Chen said, "The Jin house has lost its discipline; the mandate has passed to the virtuous; both our states have received the bright mandate in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Chen said, "The Jin house has lost its way; the mandate has passed to the worthy; both our realms have received Heaven's mandate in turn.

sentences.zh: 而桓溫猖狂，窺我王略，燕危秦孤，勢不獨立，是以秦主同恤時患，要結好援。

translations.literal: Yet Huan Wen is reckless and eyes our royal domain; Yan is endangered and Qin isolated—we cannot stand alone, so the King of Qin shares our present distress and has sought a bond of alliance.
translations.idiomatic: But Huan Wen is reckless and eyes our lands; Yan is in peril and Qin stands alone, so the King of Qin shares our distress and has sought alliance.

sentences.zh: 東朝君臣，引領西望，愧其不競，以為鄰憂，西使之辱，敬待有加。

translations.literal: The ruler and ministers of the eastern court stretch their necks looking west, ashamed at their lack of vigor and taking it as a neighbor's worry; the insult to the western envoy should be met with added respect.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern court looks west in shame at its weakness; your envoy's slight should be answered with greater courtesy.

sentences.zh: 今強寇既退，交聘方始，謂宜崇禮篤義以固二國之歡；

translations.literal: Now that the strong foe has withdrawn and exchanges have just begun, it is fitting to exalt ritual and deepen righteousness to secure the joy of both states;
translations.idiomatic: Now that the great enemy has withdrawn and embassies have begun, you should honor ritual and deepen goodwill between our states;

sentences.zh: 若忽慢使臣，是卑燕也，豈修好之義乎！

translations.literal: if you slight the envoy, you demean Yan—is that the meaning of seeking good relations!
translations.idiomatic: to slight the envoy is to demean Yan—is that how you keep friendship!

sentences.zh: 夫天子以四海為家，故行曰乘輿，止曰行在。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his home; hence in motion he is called 'imperial carriage,' at rest 'where the procession halts.'
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven makes the four seas his home; on the move he is the imperial carriage, at rest the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 今寓縣瓜裂，天光分曜，安得以乘輿、行在為言哉！

translations.literal: Now the realm is split like a melon and heaven's light divided—how can one still speak of 'imperial carriage' and 'traveling palace'!
translations.idiomatic: The realm is split and rival courts shine separately—how can one still speak of imperial carriage and traveling palace!

sentences.zh: 禮，不期而見曰遇；

translations.literal: In ritual, a meeting not arranged in advance is called an encounter;
translations.idiomatic: In ritual, a meeting not arranged in advance is called an encounter;

sentences.zh: 蓋因事權行，其禮簡略，豈平居容與之所為哉！

translations.literal: it is done expediently because circumstances require it, and the rite is brief—is that what one does in leisurely daily intercourse!
translations.idiomatic: it is done expediently when circumstances demand, and the rite is brief—is that what one does in ordinary court life!

sentences.zh: 客使單行，誠勢屈於主人；

translations.literal: An envoy traveling alone is indeed in a position subordinate to the host;
translations.idiomatic: An envoy traveling alone is indeed at the host's mercy;

sentences.zh: 然苟不以禮，亦不敢從也。」

translations.literal: yet if there is no proper ritual, I also dare not comply."
translations.idiomatic: yet without proper ritual, I dare not comply."

sentences.zh: 堅乃為之設行宮，百僚倍位，然後延客，如燕朝之儀。

translations.literal: Jian then set up a traveling palace for him, doubled the ranks of officials, and only then received the guest according to Yan court ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Jian then set up a traveling palace, doubled the ranks of officials, and received Chen with Yan court ceremony.

sentences.zh: 事畢，堅與之私宴，問：「東朝名臣為誰？」

translations.literal: When the business was done, Jian gave him a private banquet and asked, "Who are the famed ministers of the eastern court?"
translations.idiomatic: When the audience ended, Jian entertained him privately and asked, "Who are the great ministers of the eastern court?"

sentences.zh: 琛曰：「太傅上庸王評，明德茂親，光輔王室；

translations.literal: Chen said, "Grand Tutor Prince of Shangyong Ping, of bright virtue and rich kinship, gloriously assists the royal house;
translations.idiomatic: Chen said, "Grand Tutor Prince of Shangyong Murong Ping, of bright virtue and royal kin, gloriously assists the throne;

sentences.zh: 車騎大將軍吳王垂，雄略冠世，折沖御侮；

translations.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Prince of Wu Chui, whose heroic strategy crowns the age and breaks enemy charges to repel insult;
translations.idiomatic: General of Chariots and Cavalry Prince of Wu Murong Chui, whose strategy crowns the age and repels every foe;

sentences.zh: 其餘或以文進，或以武用，官皆稱職，野無遺賢。」

translations.literal: the rest advance by literary talent or are employed for martial skill; every office is filled by the capable, and no worthy man is left in the wilds."
translations.idiomatic: the rest rise by civil or military merit; every post is filled, and no talent is wasted in the fields."

sentences.zh: 琛從兄弈為秦尚書郎，堅使典客館琛於弈捨。

translations.literal: Chen's cousin Yi was a master of writing in Qin; Jian had the reception office lodge Chen at Yi's house.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's cousin Murong Yi was a master of writing in Qin; Jian had the reception office lodge Chen at Yi's house.

sentences.zh: 琛曰：「昔諸葛瑾為吳聘蜀，與諸葛亮惟公朝相見，退無私面，余竊慕之。

translations.literal: Chen said, "Formerly Zhuge Jin went on mission from Wu to Shu and met Zhuge Liang only at court; in private they did not meet—I have secretly admired that.
translations.idiomatic: Chen said, "When Zhuge Jin went from Wu to Shu, he met Zhuge Liang only at court and never in private—I have always admired that.

sentences.zh: 今使之即安私室，所不敢也。」

translations.literal: To have me lodge at once in a private house—I dare not."
translations.idiomatic: To lodge me in a private house at once—I cannot accept."

sentences.zh: 乃不果館。

translations.literal: He was therefore not lodged there after all.
translations.idiomatic: So he was not lodged there.

sentences.zh: 弈數來就邸捨，與琛臥起，閒問琛東國事。

translations.literal: Yi came often to the guest house, sharing Chen's rising and sleeping, and in idle moments asked about affairs in the eastern state.
translations.idiomatic: Yi visited the guest house often, sharing Chen's daily life and asking in private about the eastern realm.

sentences.zh: 琛曰：「今二方分據，兄弟並蒙榮龐，論其本心，各有所在。

translations.literal: Chen said, "Now the two sides hold separate territories; we brothers both enjoy honor and favor, but in our hearts each has his own allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Chen said, "Our two realms are divided; we brothers both enjoy honor, but our hearts belong to different masters.

sentences.zh: 琛欲言東國之美，恐非西國之所欲聞；

translations.literal: If I speak of the eastern state's virtues, I fear that is not what the western state wishes to hear;
translations.idiomatic: If I praise the east, the west may not wish to hear it;

sentences.zh: 欲言其惡，又非使臣之所得論也。

translations.literal: if I speak of its faults, that is not what an envoy may discuss.
translations.idiomatic: if I speak of its faults, that is not for an envoy to discuss.

sentences.zh: 兄何用問為！」

translations.literal: Why ask, brother!"
translations.idiomatic: Why ask at all, brother!"

sentences.zh: 堅使太子延琛相見。

translations.literal: Jian had the crown prince extend an audience to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had the crown prince receive Chen.

sentences.zh: 秦人欲使琛拜太子，先諷之曰：「鄰國之君，猶其君也；

translations.literal: The Qin people wished Chen to bow to the crown prince and first hinted: "A neighboring state's ruler is like one's own ruler;
translations.idiomatic: The Qin wanted Chen to bow to the crown prince and hinted, "A neighboring ruler is like one's own ruler;

sentences.zh: 鄰國之儲君，亦何以異乎！」

translations.literal: how should a neighboring heir be any different!"
translations.idiomatic: how should a neighboring heir be different!"

sentences.zh: 琛曰：「天子之子視元士，欲其由賤以登貴也。

translations.literal: Chen said, "The Son of Heaven's sons are regarded as starting from the lowest officer rank so they may rise from humble to noble.
translations.idiomatic: Chen said, "The Son of Heaven's sons begin as the lowest officers so they may rise from humble to high rank.

sentences.zh: 尚不敢臣其父之臣，況它國之臣乎！

translations.literal: They do not even dare make ministers of their father's ministers—how much less ministers of another state!
translations.idiomatic: They do not even treat their father's ministers as subjects—how much less another state's ministers!

sentences.zh: 苟無純敬，則禮有往來，情豈忘恭，但恐降屈為煩耳。」

translations.literal: Without pure reverence, ritual still has its exchanges; feeling does not forget respect, but I fear the trouble of bowing low."
translations.idiomatic: Without full reverence, ritual still allows exchange; respect remains, but I fear the bother of repeated prostration."

sentences.zh: 乃不果拜。

translations.literal: He therefore did not bow after all.
translations.idiomatic: So he did not bow.

sentences.zh: 王猛勸堅留琛，堅不許。

translations.literal: Wang Meng urged Jian to detain Chen; Jian would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng urged Jian to keep Chen; Jian refused.

sentences.zh: 燕主暐遣大鴻臚溫統拜袁真使持節、都督淮南諸軍事、征南大將軍、揚州刺史，封宣城公。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Wei sent Grand Herald Wen Tong to invest Yuan Zhen as commissioner with full powers, supervisor of military affairs in Huainan, Grand General Who Campaigns South, governor of Yang Province, and enfeoff him as Duke of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei sent Grand Herald Wen Tong to invest Yuan Zhen as commissioner with full powers, commander of Huainan, Grand General Who Campaigns South, governor of Yang Province, and Duke of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 統未逾淮而卒。

translations.literal: Tong died before crossing the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Tong died before he crossed the Huai.

sentences.zh: 吳王垂自襄邑還鄴，威名益振，太傅評愈忌之。

translations.literal: Prince of Wu Chui returned from Xiangyi to Ye; his fame grew ever greater and Grand Tutor Ping hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wu Murong Chui returned from Xiangyi to Ye; his fame grew and Grand Tutor Murong Ping hated him all the more.

sentences.zh: 垂奏：「所募將士忘身立效，將軍孫蓋等摧鋒陷陳，應蒙殊賞。」

translations.literal: Chui memorialized: "The soldiers I recruited risked their lives and achieved merit; Generals Sun Gai and others broke the enemy vanguard and pierced the battle lines—they should receive extraordinary rewards."
translations.idiomatic: Chui memorialized, "The troops I raised risked their lives; Generals Sun Gai and others broke the enemy line and deserve exceptional reward."

sentences.zh: 評皆抑而不行。

translations.literal: Ping suppressed all of these and would not act.
translations.idiomatic: Ping blocked every request.

sentences.zh: 垂數以為言，與評廷爭，怨隙愈深。

translations.literal: Chui spoke of it repeatedly and quarreled with Ping at court; their enmity grew deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Chui pressed the matter repeatedly and quarreled with Ping at court; their hatred deepened.

sentences.zh: 太後可足渾氏素惡垂，毀其戰功，與評密謀誅之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Lady Kezuhun had long hated Chui, slandered his battle achievements, and secretly plotted with Ping to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Lady Kezuhun had long hated Chui, belittled his victories, and secretly plotted with Ping to kill him.

sentences.zh: 太宰恪之子楷及垂舅蘭建知之，以告垂曰：「先發制人，但除評及樂安王臧，餘無能為矣。」

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Ke's son Kai and Chui's uncle Lan Jian learned of it and told Chui: "Strike first—remove only Ping and Prince of Le'an Zang, and the rest can do nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke's son Murong Kai and Chui's uncle Lan Jian learned of it and told Chui, "Strike first—remove Ping and Prince of Le'an Murong Zang, and the rest are helpless."

sentences.zh: 垂曰：「骨肉相殘而首亂於國，吾有死而已，不忍為也。」

translations.literal: Chui said, "Kin slaughtering kin and being first to throw the state into chaos—I would rather die than do that."
translations.idiomatic: Chui said, "Kin killing kin and being first to throw the realm into chaos—I would rather die than do that."

sentences.zh: 頃之，二人又以告，曰：「內意已決，不可不早發。」

translations.literal: Shortly after, the two told him again: "Their minds within are already set—you must not delay striking."
translations.idiomatic: Soon they warned him again, "Their minds are made up—you must act at once."

sentences.zh: 垂曰：「必不可彌縫，吾寧避之於外，餘非所議。」

translations.literal: Chui said, "This cannot be patched over; I would rather withdraw abroad—that is all I will consider."
translations.idiomatic: Chui said, "This cannot be patched; I would rather withdraw abroad—that is all I will consider."

sentences.zh: 垂內以為憂，而未敢告諸子。

translations.literal: Chui was inwardly troubled but did not yet dare tell his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Chui was inwardly troubled but had not yet told his sons.

sentences.zh: 世子令請曰：「尊比者如有憂色，豈非以主上幼沖，太傅疾賢，功高望重，愈見猜邪？」

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Ling asked permission to speak: "Father, of late you seem troubled—is it not because the ruler is young, the Grand Tutor envies the worthy, and your high merit and great renown draw ever more suspicion?"
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Murong Ling asked, "Father, you have looked troubled lately—is it because the ruler is young, the Grand Tutor envies talent, and your great merit draws ever more suspicion?"

sentences.zh: 垂曰：「然。

translations.literal: Chui said, "It is so.
translations.idiomatic: Chui said, "It is.

sentences.zh: 吾竭力致命以破強寇，本欲保全家國，豈知功成之後，返令身無所容。

translations.literal: I exhausted my strength and risked my life to break the strong foe, intending to preserve family and state—who knew that after success I would have nowhere to stand.
translations.idiomatic: I risked everything to break the great enemy to save family and state—who knew that after success I would have nowhere to stand.

sentences.zh: 汝既知吾心，何以為吾謀？」

translations.literal: Now that you know my mind, what will you advise?"
translations.idiomatic: You know my mind—what do you advise?"

sentences.zh: 令曰：「主上闇弱，委任太傅，一旦禍發，疾於駭機。

translations.literal: Ling said, "The ruler is dim and weak and has entrusted everything to the Grand Tutor; once disaster strikes it will be swifter than a triggered crossbow.
translations.idiomatic: Ling said, "The ruler is weak and has entrusted everything to the Grand Tutor; once disaster strikes it will be faster than a sprung trap.

sentences.zh: 今欲保族全身，不失大義，莫若逃之龍城，遜辭謝罪，以待主上之察，若周公之居東，庶幾可以感寤而得還，此幸之大者也。

translations.literal: To preserve the clan and your person without losing righteousness, nothing is better than fleeing to Longcheng, yielding with humble words and apology, and waiting for the ruler's discernment—like the Duke of Zhou's stay in the east; perhaps you may move him to understanding and return. That would be the greatest good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: To save the clan and yourself without losing righteousness, flee to Longcheng, submit a humble apology, and wait for the ruler's judgment—like the Duke of Zhou in the east; perhaps he will understand and recall you. That would be the best outcome.

sentences.zh: 如其不然，則內撫燕、代，外懷群夷，守肥如之險以自保，亦其次也。」

translations.literal: If not, then pacify Yan and Dai within, win the various tribes without, and hold the perilous passes at Feiru to preserve yourself—that is the next best."
translations.idiomatic: If not, pacify Yan and Dai within, win the tribes without, and hold the passes at Feiru—that is the next best."

sentences.zh: 垂曰：「善！」

translations.literal: Chui said, "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: Chui said, "Well said!"

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛亥朔，垂請畋於大陸，因微服出鄴，將趨龍城。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the new moon of xinhai, Chui asked to hunt on the mainland and, in disguise, left Ye intending to make for Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the new moon of xinhai, Chui asked to hunt on the mainland and slipped out of Ye in disguise, heading for Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 至邯鄲，少子麟，素不為垂所愛，逃還告狀，垂左右多亡叛。

translations.literal: At Handan his youngest son Lin, whom Chui had never favored, fled back to report; many of Chui's attendants deserted.
translations.idiomatic: At Handan his youngest son Murong Lin, whom Chui had never favored, fled back to inform on him; many of his attendants deserted.

sentences.zh: 太傅評白燕主暐，遣西平公強帥精騎追之，及於范陽。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Ping informed the Yan ruler Wei, who sent Prince of Xiping Qiang with crack cavalry in pursuit; they caught up at Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Ping informed Murong Wei, who sent Prince of Xiping Murong Qiang with elite cavalry in pursuit; they caught up at Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 世子令斷後，強不敢逼。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Ling covered the rear; Qiang did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Ling covered the rear; Qiang did not dare press him.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，令謂垂曰：「本欲保東都以自全，今事已洩，謀不及設。

translations.literal: As night fell, Ling said to Chui: "We meant to hold the eastern capital to preserve ourselves; now the affair is exposed and plans cannot be laid in time.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Ling told Chui, "We meant to hold the eastern capital to survive; now the secret is out and there is no time to plan.

sentences.zh: 秦主方招延英傑，不如往歸之。」

translations.literal: The King of Qin is recruiting heroes—better to go submit to him."
translations.idiomatic: The King of Qin is gathering heroes—better to go to him."

sentences.zh: 垂曰：「今日之計，捨此安之！」

translations.literal: Chui said, "For today's plan, where else can we go but this!"
translations.idiomatic: Chui said, "For today, where else can we turn!"

sentences.zh: 乃散騎滅跡，傍南山復還鄴，隱於趙之顯原陵。

translations.literal: They then scattered their riders and erased their tracks, followed the southern hills back toward Ye, and hid at Xianyuan Tomb in Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: They scattered their riders, erased their tracks, followed the southern hills back toward Ye, and hid at Xianyuan Tomb in Zhao.

sentences.zh: 俄有獵者數百騎四面而來，抗之則不能敵，逃之則無路，不知所為。

translations.literal: Soon several hundred mounted hunters came from all sides; to resist was impossible, to flee there was no road—they knew not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Soon several hundred mounted hunters closed in from all sides; they could neither fight nor flee.

sentences.zh: 會獵者鷹皆飛揚，眾騎散去。

translations.literal: Just then the hunters' hawks all flew up, and the riders dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the hunters' hawks all flew up, and the riders dispersed.

sentences.zh: 垂乃殺白馬以祭天，且盟從者。

translations.literal: Chui then killed a white horse to sacrifice to Heaven and swore an oath with his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Chui killed a white horse to sacrifice to Heaven and swore an oath with his followers.

sentences.zh: 世子令言於垂曰：「太傅忌賢疾能，構事以來，人尤忿恨。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Ling said to Chui: "The Grand Tutor envies the worthy and hates ability; since he began this affair, people are especially resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Ling told Chui, "The Grand Tutor envies talent; since he began this plot, the people are furious.

sentences.zh: 今鄴城之中，莫知尊處，如嬰兒之思母，夷、夏同之。

translations.literal: Now in Ye no one knows where you are; like infants longing for their mother, barbarian and Chinese alike feel the same.
translations.idiomatic: In Ye no one knows where you are; barbarian and Chinese alike long for you like children for their mother.

sentences.zh: 若順眾心，襲其無備，取之如指掌耳。

translations.literal: If you follow the people's hearts and strike while they are unprepared, taking the city will be like reading your palm.
translations.idiomatic: Follow the people's will and strike while they are unprepared—you will take the city as easily as turning your hand.

sentences.zh: 事定之後，革弊簡能，大匡朝政，以輔主上，安國存家，功之大者也。

translations.literal: When the affair is settled, reform abuses, promote the capable, greatly rectify court governance, assist the ruler, and secure state and family—that would be the greatest achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When it is done, reform abuses, promote the capable, set the court right, assist the ruler, and save state and family—that would be your greatest achievement.

sentences.zh: 今日之便，誠不可失，願給騎數人，足以辦之。」

translations.literal: Today's opportunity truly must not be lost; grant me a few horsemen and it will be enough to accomplish it."
translations.idiomatic: Today's chance must not be lost; give me a few horsemen and it will be enough."

sentences.zh: 垂曰：「如汝之謀，事成誠為大福，不成悔之何及！

translations.literal: Chui said, "If your plan succeeds it is indeed great fortune; if it fails, regret will come too late!
translations.idiomatic: Chui said, "If your plan succeeds it is great fortune; if it fails, regret will be too late!

sentences.zh: 不如西奔，可以萬全。」

translations.literal: Better to flee west—that can be wholly secure."
translations.idiomatic: Better to flee west—that alone is safe."

sentences.zh: 子馬奴潛謀逃歸，殺之而行。

translations.literal: His son Manu secretly plotted to flee home; they killed him and went on.
translations.idiomatic: His son Manu secretly plotted to flee home; they killed him and marched on.

sentences.zh: 至河陽，為津吏所禁，斬之而濟。

translations.literal: At Heyang a ferry officer barred them; they killed him and crossed.
translations.idiomatic: At Heyang a ferry officer barred them; they killed him and crossed.

sentences.zh: 遂自洛陽與段夫人、世子令、令弟寶、農、隆、兄子楷、舅蘭建、郎中令高弼俱奔秦，留妃可足渾氏於鄴。

translations.literal: They then went from Luoyang with Lady Duan, Heir Apparent Ling, Ling's brothers Bao, Nong, and Long, his brother's son Kai, his uncle Lan Jian, and director of attendants Gao Bi—all fled to Qin, leaving Consort Lady Kezuhun in Ye.
translations.idiomatic: From Luoyang they fled to Qin with Lady Duan, Heir Apparent Ling, his brothers Bao, Nong, and Long, his nephew Kai, his uncle Lan Jian, and director of attendants Gao Bi, leaving Consort Lady Kezuhun in Ye.

sentences.zh: 乙泉戌主吳歸追及於闅鄉，世子令擊之而退。

translations.literal: Wu Gui, commander of Yiquan Garrison, overtook them at Wuxiang; Heir Apparent Ling struck and drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Gui, commander of Yiquan Garrison, overtook them at Wuxiang; Heir Apparent Ling drove him back.

sentences.zh: 初，秦王堅聞太宰恪卒，陰有圖燕之志，憚垂威名，不敢發。

translations.literal: Earlier, when King of Qin Fu Jian heard that Grand Preceptor Ke had died, he secretly harbored the will to take Yan but feared Chui's renown and did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when King Fu Jian heard that Grand Preceptor Murong Ke had died, he secretly planned to conquer Yan but feared Murong Chui's fame and held back.

sentences.zh: 及聞垂至，大喜，郊迎，執手曰：「天生賢傑，必相與共成大功，此自然之數也。

translations.literal: When he heard Chui had arrived he was greatly pleased, met him in the suburbs, took his hand and said, "Heaven-born worthies must together achieve great deeds—this is the natural order.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Chui had come he was delighted, met him outside the city, took his hand and said, "Heaven sends great men to achieve great things together—that is nature's way.

sentences.zh: 要當與卿共定天下，告成岱宗，然後還卿本邦，世封幽州，使卿去國不失為子之孝，歸朕不失事君之忠，不亦美乎！」

translations.literal: I mean to settle the realm with you, report success at Mount Tai, then return you to your native state with hereditary enfeoffment in You Province, so that in leaving your country you do not lose filial piety and in returning to me you do not lose loyalty as subject—is that not fine!"
translations.idiomatic: I mean to settle the realm with you, report success at Mount Tai, then return you to your homeland with hereditary rule in You Province, so you keep filial piety toward your state and loyalty toward me—is that not fine!"

sentences.zh: 垂謝曰；

translations.literal: Chui thanked him and said;
translations.idiomatic: Chui thanked him and said;

sentences.zh: 「羈旅之臣，免罪為幸。

translations.literal: "A wanderer in exile—escape from punishment is already fortune.
translations.idiomatic: "A wanderer in exile—to escape punishment is fortune enough.

sentences.zh: 本邦之榮，非所敢望！」

translations.literal: Glory in my native state—I dare not hope for it!"
translations.idiomatic: Glory in my homeland—I dare not hope for it!"

sentences.zh: 堅復愛世子令及慕容楷之才，皆厚禮之，賞賜巨萬，每進見，屬目觀之。

translations.literal: Jian also admired the talents of Heir Apparent Ling and Murong Kai, treated both with generous ritual, rewarded them with tens of thousands, and whenever they came to audience fixed his gaze upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Jian also admired Heir Apparent Ling and Murong Kai, treated them generously, rewarded them lavishly, and watched them closely whenever they came to court.

sentences.zh: 關中士民素聞垂父子名，皆向慕之。

translations.literal: The gentry and commoners of Guanzhong had long heard the names of Chui and his sons and all turned toward them in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guanzhong had long heard of Chui and his sons and admired them.

sentences.zh: 王猛言於堅曰：「慕容垂父子，譬如龍虎，非可馴之物，若借以風雲，將不可複製，不如早除之。」

translations.literal: Wang Meng said to Jian: "Murong Chui and his sons are like dragon and tiger—not creatures that can be tamed; if you lend them wind and cloud, they cannot be caught again. Better to remove them early."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng told Jian, "Murong Chui and his sons are dragon and tiger—not creatures to tame; give them wind and cloud and you cannot catch them again. Better remove them early."

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「吾方收攬英雄以清四海，奈何殺之！

translations.literal: Jian said, "I am just gathering heroes to clear the four seas—how can I kill them!
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "I am gathering heroes to pacify the realm—how can I kill them!

sentences.zh: 且其始來，吾已推誠納之矣。

translations.literal: Moreover when they first came I received them with open sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: When they first came I received them in good faith.

sentences.zh: 匹夫猶不棄言，況萬乘乎！」

translations.literal: Even a common man does not break his word—how much less one who rides ten thousand chariots!"
translations.idiomatic: Even a common man keeps his word—how much less an emperor!"

sentences.zh: 乃以垂為冠軍將軍，封賓徒侯，楷為積弩將軍。

translations.literal: He then made Chui General Who Establishes Might and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Bintu, and made Kai General of Strong Crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: He made Chui General Who Establishes Might and Marquis of Bintu, and Kai General of Strong Crossbows.

sentences.zh: 燕魏尹范陽王德素與垂善，及車騎從事中郎高泰等，皆坐免官。

translations.literal: Yan's metropolitan governor Prince of Fanyang De had long been friendly with Chui; he and attendant cavalier of the chariots and cavalry Gao Tai and others were all dismissed from office on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's metropolitan governor Prince of Fanyang Murong De had long been friendly with Chui; he and attendant cavalier Gao Tai and others were all dismissed on account of it.

sentences.zh: 尚書右丞申紹言於太傅評曰：「今吳王出奔，外口籍籍，宜征王僚屬之賢者顯進之，粗可消謗。」

translations.literal: Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Shen Shao said to Grand Tutor Ping: "Now that the Prince of Wu has fled, rumor runs outside; you should summon worthy men among the prince's staff and promote them visibly—roughly that can quiet slander."
translations.idiomatic: Right assistant director Shen Shao told Grand Tutor Ping, "With the Prince of Wu in flight, rumor runs wild; promote worthy men from his staff and you may quiet the talk."

sentences.zh: 評曰：「誰可者？」

translations.literal: Ping said, "Who would do?"
translations.idiomatic: Ping said, "Who would serve?"

sentences.zh: 紹曰：「高泰其領袖也。」

translations.literal: Shao said, "Gao Tai is their leader."
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "Gao Tai is their leader."

sentences.zh: 乃以泰為尚書郎。

translations.literal: He then appointed Tai as a master of writing attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was then made master of writing attendant.

sentences.zh: 泰，瞻之從子；

translations.literal: Tai was Zhan's nephew;
translations.idiomatic: Tai was Shen Zhan's nephew;

sentences.zh: 紹，胤之兄也。

translations.literal: Shao was Yin's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was the elder brother of Shen Yin.

sentences.zh: 秦留梁琛月餘，乃遣歸。

translations.literal: Qin detained Liang Chen for more than a month, then sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin kept Liang Chen over a month before letting him return.

sentences.zh: 琛兼程而進，比至鄴，吳王垂已奔秦。

translations.literal: Chen pressed on day and night; by the time he reached Ye, Prince of Wu Chui had already fled to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Chen pushed on without rest, but by the time he reached Ye, Prince of Wu Murong Chui had already defected to Qin.

sentences.zh: 琛言於太傅評曰：「秦人日閱軍旅，多聚糧於陝東。

translations.literal: Chen said to Grand Tutor Ping: "The men of Qin review their armies daily and gather much grain east of Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen told Grand Tutor Murong Ping, "Qin drills its troops every day and is stockpiling grain east of Shan.

sentences.zh: 以琛觀之，為和必不能久。

translations.literal: In Chen's view, peace cannot last long.
translations.idiomatic: In my view, this peace will not hold for long.

sentences.zh: 今吳王又往歸之，秦必有窺燕之謀，宜早為之備。」

translations.literal: Now the Prince of Wu has again gone to join them; Qin surely plans to spy on Yan—preparations ought to be made early."
translations.idiomatic: Now Prince of Wu Murong Chui has gone over as well; Qin surely intends to move against Yan, and we should prepare without delay."

sentences.zh: 評曰：「秦豈肯受叛臣而敗和好哉！」

translations.literal: Ping said, "Would Qin willingly accept a rebel minister and ruin the friendship!"
translations.idiomatic: Ping said, "Why would Qin shelter a traitor and wreck the alliance between our states!"

sentences.zh: 琛曰：「今二國分據中原，常有相吞之志。

translations.literal: Chen said, "The two states now partition the Central Plains and constantly harbor the will to swallow each other.
translations.idiomatic: Chen said, "The two realms divide the heartland, and each has long wanted to devour the other.

sentences.zh: 桓溫之入寇，彼以計相救，非愛燕也。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen invaded, they aided us by calculation, not from love of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen invaded, Qin helped us by design, not out of any love for Yan.

sentences.zh: 若燕有釁，彼豈忘其本志哉！」

translations.literal: If Yan shows an opening, how could they forget their original aim!"
translations.idiomatic: If Yan shows weakness, how would they forget what they wanted all along!"

sentences.zh: 評曰：「秦主何如人？」

translations.literal: Ping said, "What manner of man is the Qin ruler?"
translations.idiomatic: Ping asked, "What sort of man is the ruler of Qin?"

sentences.zh: 琛曰：「明而善斷。」

translations.literal: Chen said, "Clear-sighted and skilled at decision."
translations.idiomatic: Chen said, "Clear-minded and decisive."

sentences.zh: 問王猛，曰：「名不虛得。」

translations.literal: When asked about Wang Meng, he said, "His fame is not unearned."
translations.idiomatic: Asked about Wang Meng, he said, "His reputation is deserved."

sentences.zh: 評皆不以為然。

translations.literal: Ping did not agree with any of it.
translations.idiomatic: Ping dismissed it all.

sentences.zh: 琛又以告燕主暐，暐亦不然之。

translations.literal: Chen also told the Yan ruler Wei, and Wei likewise did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Chen reported the same to Murong Wei, who was equally unconvinced.

sentences.zh: 以告皇甫真，真深憂之，上疏言：「苻堅雖聘問相尋，然實有窺上國之心，非能慕樂德義，不忘久要也。

translations.literal: He also told Huangfu Zhen; Zhen was deeply troubled and submitted a memorial saying: "Though Fu Jian sends envoys in unbroken succession, he truly has the mind to spy on the upper kingdom; he is not one who can admire virtue and righteousness and not forget an old compact.
translations.idiomatic: He told Huangfu Zhen as well; Zhen was deeply alarmed and memorialized: "Though Fu Jian keeps up a stream of courtesy missions, he is really scheming against our realm—he does not truly admire our virtue or honor an old alliance.

sentences.zh: 前出兵洛川，及使者繼至，國之險易虛實，彼皆得之矣。

translations.literal: Earlier troops were sent to the Luo River, and as envoys followed one after another, the adversary has learned all the state's defiles, level ground, strength, and weakness.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier advance to the Luo River and the envoys who followed have taught them our defenses, terrain, and true condition.

sentences.zh: 今吳王垂又往從之，為其謀主；

translations.literal: Now Prince of Wu Chui has again gone to join them and become their chief strategist;
translations.idiomatic: Now Prince of Wu Murong Chui has gone over and serves as their chief strategist;

sentences.zh: 伍員之禍，不可不備。

translations.literal: The disaster of Wu Yuan cannot go unprepared for.
translations.idiomatic: The calamity of Wu Zixu is a warning we cannot ignore.

sentences.zh: 洛陽、太原、壺關，皆宜選將益兵，以防未然。」

translations.literal: Luoyang, Taiyuan, and Huguan should all have generals chosen and troops added to guard against what has not yet happened."
translations.idiomatic: We should assign stronger garrisons at Luoyang, Taiyuan, and Huguan before trouble appears."

sentences.zh: 暐召太傅評謀之，評曰：「秦國小力弱，恃我為援；

translations.literal: Wei summoned Grand Tutor Ping to consult; Ping said, "Qin's state is small and its strength weak—it relies on us as its support;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei summoned Grand Tutor Ping to discuss it; Ping said, "Qin is small and weak and depends on us for support;

sentences.zh: 且苻堅庶幾善道，終不肯納叛臣之言，絕二國之好。

translations.literal: Moreover Fu Jian is somewhat on the path of goodness and in the end would not heed the words of a rebel minister and break the two states' friendship.
translations.idiomatic: and Fu Jian is at least a decent ruler—he would never listen to a defector and rupture our friendship.

sentences.zh: 不宜輕自驚擾以啟寇心。」

translations.literal: One should not lightly alarm and disturb oneself and thus arouse the enemy's appetite."
translations.idiomatic: We should not panic and provoke an enemy appetite."

sentences.zh: 卒不為備。

translations.literal: In the end they made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they prepared nothing.

sentences.zh: 秦遣黃門郎石越聘於燕，太傅評示之以奢，欲以誇燕之富盛。

translations.literal: Qin sent yellow gate attendant Shi Yue on a mission to Yan; Grand Tutor Ping displayed luxury before him, intending to boast of Yan's wealth and splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Qin sent attendant Shi Yue of the yellow gate as envoy to Yan, and Grand Tutor Ping paraded luxury before him to show off Yan's riches.

sentences.zh: 高泰及太傅參軍河間劉靖言於評曰：「越言誕而視遠，非求好也，乃觀釁也。

translations.literal: Gao Tai and Grand Tutor staff officer Liu Jing of Hejian said to Ping: "Yue's words are boastful and his gaze is distant—he does not seek friendship but watches for an opening.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tai and the grand tutor's staff officer Liu Jing of Hejian told Ping, "Yue talks big and looks everywhere but friendship—he is scouting for weakness.

sentences.zh: 宜耀兵以示之，用折其謀。

translations.literal: Troops ought to be displayed to show strength and thereby break his design.
translations.idiomatic: We should parade the army to deter him and frustrate his plan.

sentences.zh: 今乃示之以奢，益為其所輕矣。」

translations.literal: Now you show him luxury instead—he will only hold you more lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Showing him luxury only makes him despise us more."

sentences.zh: 評不從。

translations.literal: Ping did not follow their advice.
translations.idiomatic: Ping refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 泰遂謝病歸。

translations.literal: Tai then pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Tai resigned citing illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 是時太后可足渾氏侵橈國政，太傅評貪昧無厭，貨賂上流，官非才舉，群下怨憤。

translations.literal: At this time Empress Dowager Kezuhun encroached on state affairs; Grand Tutor Ping was greedy beyond satiation, bribes flowed upward, offices were not filled by talent, and all below resented and raged.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Empress Dowager Kezuhun meddled in government, Grand Tutor Murong Ping was insatiably corrupt, posts went to bribery not talent, and the court seethed with resentment.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞申紹上疏，以為：「守宰者，致治之本。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Shen Shao submitted a memorial, holding: "Governors and magistrates are the root of bringing order.
translations.idiomatic: Left assistant director Shen Shao memorialized the throne: "Local administrators are the foundation of good government.

sentences.zh: 今之守宰，率非其人，或武人出於行伍，或貴戚生長綺紈，既非鄉曲之選，又不更朝廷之職。

translations.literal: Today's governors and magistrates are mostly not the right men—some are military men raised from the ranks, some noble kin bred in brocade and silk; they are neither chosen by local reputation nor rotated through court offices.
translations.idiomatic: Today's prefects are mostly unfit—some are soldiers pulled from the ranks, others pampered kinsmen who never held court office or earned local trust.

sentences.zh: 加之黜陟無法，貪惰者無刑罰之懼，清修者無旌賞之勸。

translations.literal: Added to this, promotion and dismissal follow no law; the greedy and lazy have no fear of punishment, and the pure and diligent have no encouragement of reward.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion and dismissal follow no rule: the greedy face no punishment, the honest win no reward.

sentences.zh: 是以百姓困弊，寇盜棄斥，綱頹紀紊，莫相糾攝。

translations.literal: Thus the common people are exhausted and distressed, bandits and robbers are everywhere, the great cord sags and ranks are tangled, and none correct or restrain one another.
translations.idiomatic: The people are exhausted, bandits roam free, law and order collapse, and no one holds anyone accountable.

sentences.zh: 又官吏猥多，逾於前世，公私紛然，不勝煩擾。

translations.literal: Moreover officials are excessively numerous, exceeding former ages; public and private affairs are in turmoil and cannot bear the vexation and harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Officials multiply beyond any previous age, and public and private life drown in pointless harassment.

sentences.zh: 大燕戶口，數兼二寇，弓馬之勁，四方莫及；

translations.literal: Great Yan's registered households equal both rival states combined, and the strength of its bowmen and horses none under heaven can match;
translations.idiomatic: Great Yan's population rivals both enemy states together, and none can match its archers and horsemen;

sentences.zh: 而比者戰則屢北，皆由守宰賦調不平，侵漁無已，行留俱窘，莫肯致命故也。

translations.literal: Yet in recent battles defeat has been repeated—all because governors and magistrates levy taxes unfairly, plunder without end, and whether on march or at rest all are hard pressed, so none will give their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Yet we lose battle after battle because local officers levy taxes unevenly and never stop extorting—soldiers at march or rest are too desperate to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 後宮之女四千餘人，僮侍廝役尚在其外，一日之費，厥直萬金。

translations.literal: Women of the rear palace number more than four thousand, and pages, attendants, and menials lie outside that count; one day's expense runs to ten thousand in gold.
translations.idiomatic: More than four thousand women fill the harem, not counting pages and servants, and the court spends ten thousand in gold every day.

sentences.zh: 士民承風，競為奢靡。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners catch the wind and vie in extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and commoners follow suit and vie in extravagance.

sentences.zh: 彼秦、吳僭僻，猶能條治所部，有兼併之心，而我上下因循，日失其序。

translations.literal: Those upstarts Qin and Wu, remote and petty though they are, can still put their domains in order and harbor the will to annex; while we above and below drift along and lose order day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Even upstart Qin and Wu keep their domains in order and scheme for conquest, while we drift day by day into disorder.

sentences.zh: 我之不修，彼之願也。

translations.literal: Our failure to put things in order is their wish.
translations.idiomatic: Our decay is exactly what they hope for.

sentences.zh: 謂宜精擇守宰，並官省職，存恤兵家，使公私兩遂，節抑浮靡，愛惜用度，賞必當功，罰必當罪。

translations.literal: It is proposed that governors and magistrates be finely chosen, offices merged and posts reduced, military households preserved and cared for so public and private interests both succeed, extravagance restrained and checked, expenditures cherished and economized, rewards given only for merit, punishments only for crime.
translations.idiomatic: Choose administrators carefully, merge offices and cut posts, relieve military households, balance public and private need, curb luxury, husband resources, reward only merit, and punish only guilt.

sentences.zh: 如此，則溫、猛可梟，二方可取，豈特保境安民而已哉！

translations.literal: If so, Wen and Meng can be displayed on poles, both directions can be taken—how would it be merely guarding borders and settling the people!
translations.idiomatic: Then Huan Wen and Wang Meng could be brought low and both Qin and Jin taken—not merely defending our borders!

sentences.zh: 又，索頭什翼犍疲病昏悖，雖乏貢御，無能為患；

translations.literal: Moreover Bald-head Shiyijian is weary, sick, muddled, and deluded; though tribute and the imperial hunt are lacking, he cannot become a danger;
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Shiyijian is feeble, sick, and senile; though tribute fails, he poses no threat;

sentences.zh: 而勞兵遠戌，有損無益。

translations.literal: Yet to weary the army with distant garrison duty has loss and no gain.
translations.idiomatic: Yet distant garrisons wear out the army to no profit.

sentences.zh: 不若移於並土，控制西河，南堅壺關，北重晉陽，西寇來則拒守，過則斷後，猶愈於戌孤城守無用之地也。」

translations.literal: Better to shift to the land of Bing, control West River, strengthen Huguan in the south and lay weight on Jinyang in the north—when western raiders come, hold them off; when they pass, cut off their rear—this is still better than garrisoning a lonely city and holding useless ground."
translations.idiomatic: Shift those forces to Bing province: hold West River, fortify Huguan in the south and Jinyang in the north—block western raids and cut off their retreat—rather than rotting in useless frontier towns."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and received no attention.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went in and was ignored.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，丞相昱與大司馬溫會塗中，以謀後舉；

translations.literal: On xinchou, Prime Minister Yu and Grand Marshal Wen met on the road to plan the next campaign;
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Prime Minister Sima Yu and Grand Marshal Huan Wen met on the road to plan their next move;

sentences.zh: 以溫世子熙為豫州刺史、假節。

translations.literal: Wen's heir Xi was made governor of Yu Province with acting regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's heir Huan Xi was made governor of Yu Province with provisional command.

sentences.zh: 初，燕人許割虎牢以西賂秦。

translations.literal: Earlier the men of Yan had promised to cede west of Hulao as a bribe to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yan had promised to cede everything west of Hulao as payment to Qin.

sentences.zh: 晉兵既退，燕人悔之，謂秦人曰：「行人失辭。

translations.literal: After Jin's army had withdrawn, the men of Yan regretted it and said to the men of Qin: "The envoy spoke wrongly.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin withdrew, Yan tried to take it back and told Qin, "Our envoy misspoke.

sentences.zh: 有國有家者，分災救患，理之常也。」

translations.literal: He who has a state and a clan shares disaster and aids distress—this is the constant principle."
translations.idiomatic: States help one another in calamity—that is only right."

sentences.zh: 秦王堅大怒，遣輔國將軍王猛、建威將軍梁成、洛州刺史鄧羌帥步騎三萬伐燕。

translations.literal: King of Qin Jian was greatly enraged and sent Assistant State General Wang Meng, General Who Establishes Might Liang Cheng, and Governor of Luo Province Deng Qiang to lead thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Yan.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian flew into a rage and sent Wang Meng, Liang Cheng, and Luo governor Deng Qiang with thirty thousand foot and horse against Yan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，進攻洛陽。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month they advanced to attack Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they marched on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 大司馬溫發徐、兗州民築廣陵城，徙鎮之。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Wen mobilized the people of Xu and Yan provinces to build the city of Guangling and shifted his headquarters there.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Huan Wen conscripted the people of Xu and Yan to build Guangling and moved his headquarters there.

sentences.zh: 時征役既頻，加之疫癘，死者什四五，百姓嗟怨。

translations.literal: At the time corvée and military levies had already been frequent; added to this were pestilence and plague, and the dead amounted to four or five in ten—the common people sighed and resented.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée was already crushing, plague followed, four or five in ten died, and the people groaned in anger.

sentences.zh: 秘書監太原孫盛作《晉春秋》，直書時事；

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Sun Sheng of Taiyuan compiled the Annals of Jin and wrote the times plainly;
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Sun Sheng of Taiyuan wrote the Annals of Jin, recording current affairs without evasion;

sentences.zh: 大司馬溫見之，怒，謂盛子曰：「枋頭誠為失利，何至乃如尊君所言！

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Wen saw it and was angry; he said to Sheng's son: "Fangtou was indeed a setback—how could it have come to what your honored father wrote!
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Huan Wen read it, grew furious, and told Sheng's son, "Fangtou was a defeat, yes—but nothing like what your father wrote!

sentences.zh: 若此史遂行，自是關君門戶事！」

translations.literal: If this history is published, that is a matter of your family's gates being shut!"
translations.idiomatic: If this book circulates, it will mean the ruin of your whole clan!"

sentences.zh: 其子遽拜謝，請改之。

translations.literal: His son immediately bowed and apologized, asking to revise it.
translations.idiomatic: His son prostrated himself at once and begged to revise it.

sentences.zh: 時盛年老家居，性方嚴，有軌度，子孫雖斑白，待之愈峻。

translations.literal: At the time Sheng was aged and lived at home; his nature was upright and stern, with strict measure—even though his descendants were gray-haired, he treated them the more severely.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was old and retired at home, upright and stern; even gray-haired descendants felt his iron rule.

sentences.zh: 至是諸子乃共號泣稽顙，請為百口切計。

translations.literal: On this occasion his sons all together wailed and knocked their foreheads to the ground, begging him to consider a plan for the hundred mouths of the clan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons then wept and kowtowed together, pleading for the sake of the whole clan.

sentences.zh: 盛大怒，不許，諸子遂私改之。

translations.literal: Sheng was greatly enraged and would not agree; the sons then secretly revised it.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng refused in fury; his sons altered the text in secret.

sentences.zh: 盛先已寫別本，傳之外國。

translations.literal: Sheng had already copied a separate draft and sent it abroad.
translations.idiomatic: But Sheng had already copied an alternate version and sent it abroad.

sentences.zh: 及孝武帝購求異書，得之於遼東人，與見本不同，遂兩存之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu sought out rare books, it was obtained from a man of Liaodong; it differed from the version in circulation, and so both were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu later sought rare books, a Liaodong man supplied a copy that differed from the circulated text, and both versions were kept.

sentences.zh: 海西公下太和五年（

translations.literal: Under the Deposed Emperor, fifth year of Taihe (
translations.idiomatic: Reign of the Deposed Emperor, Taihe year five (

sentences.zh: 庚午，公元三七零年）

translations.literal: gengwu, AD 370)
translations.idiomatic: year gengwu, 370 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己亥，袁真以梁國內史沛郡朱憲及弟汝南內史斌陰通大司馬溫，殺之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jihai, Yuan Zhen, because Zhu Xian of Pei commandery, interior administrator of Liang, and his younger brother Bin, interior administrator of Runan, had secretly communicated with Grand Marshal Wen, executed them.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jihai, Yuan Zhen executed Zhu Xian, interior administrator of Liang, and his brother Bin, interior administrator of Runan, for secretly dealing with Grand Marshal Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 秦王猛遺燕荊州刺史武威王築書曰：「國家今已塞成皋之險，杜盟津之路，大駕虎旅百萬，自軹關取鄴都，金墉窮戍，外無救援，城下之師，將軍所監，豈三百弊卒所能支也！」

translations.literal: Wang Meng of Qin sent a letter to Yan's Governor of Jing Province Prince of Wuwei Zhu, saying: "The state has now blocked the peril of Chenggao and shut the road at Meng Ford; the great host of tiger troops in the hundreds of thousands will take the capital of Ye through Zhiguan; the exhausted garrison at Jinyong has no relief from outside—the army beneath the walls is under the general's watch—how could three hundred worn-out soldiers support it!"
