translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng of Qin wrote Yan's Jing governor Prince of Wuwei Murong Zhu: "We have sealed Chenggao and closed Meng Ford; a million tiger troops will take Ye through Zhiguan; your exhausted garrison at Jinyong has no help—the army at the walls is yours to command—can three hundred worn men hold them!"

sentences.zh: 築懼，以洛陽降，猛陳師受之。

translations.literal: Zhu was afraid and surrendered Luoyang; Meng arrayed his army and accepted the surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zhu, terrified, surrendered Luoyang; Wang Meng formed ranks and accepted.

sentences.zh: 燕衛大將軍樂安王臧城新樂，破秦兵於石門，執秦將楊猛。

translations.literal: Yan's Guard Grand General Prince of Le'an Zang walled Xinyue, defeated Qin troops at Shimen, and captured Qin general Yang Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's Guard Grand General Prince of Le'an Murong Zang fortified Xinyue, routed Qin at Shimen, and captured Qin general Yang Meng.

sentences.zh: 王猛之發長安也，請慕容令參其軍事，以為鄉導。

translations.literal: When Wang Meng set out from Chang'an, he requested Murong Ling to join his military counsel as a native guide.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Meng marched from Chang'an, he asked Murong Ling to serve in his staff as guide through Yan country.

sentences.zh: 將行，造慕容垂飲酒，從容謂垂曰：「今當遠別，卿何以贈我，使我睹物思人？」

translations.literal: About to depart, he visited Murong Chui to drink wine and said at ease to Chui: "We are about to part far apart—what will you give me so that seeing the object I may think of the man?"
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving he visited Murong Chui for wine and said gently, "We part for a long journey—what gift will you leave me, that I may see it and think of you?"

sentences.zh: 垂脫佩刀贈之。

translations.literal: Chui removed his girdle knife and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui took off his belt knife and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 猛至洛陽，賂垂所親金熙，使詐為垂使者，謂令曰：「吾父子來此，以逃死也。

translations.literal: When Meng reached Luoyang, he bribed Chui's close associate Jin Xi and had him falsely pose as Chui's envoy, saying to Ling: "My father and I came here to escape death.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang Wang Meng bribed Murong Chui's confidant Jin Xi to pose as Chui's messenger and tell Ling, "My father and I came here only to escape death.

sentences.zh: 今王猛疾人如仇，讒毀日深；

translations.literal: Now Wang Meng hates men like an enemy, and slander grows deeper day by day;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng now hates us like enemies, and slander mounts daily;

sentences.zh: 秦王雖外相厚善，其心難知。

translations.literal: Though the King of Qin is outwardly thick and kind, his heart is hard to know.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian seems gracious on the surface, but his mind is unreadable.

sentences.zh: 丈夫逃死而卒不免，將為天下笑。

translations.literal: A true man who flees death and in the end cannot escape will become the laughter of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: A man who fled death only to die anyway will be mocked by the world.

sentences.zh: 吾聞東朝比來始更悔悟，主、後相尤。

translations.literal: I hear the Eastern Court has only lately begun to repent and awaken; lord and consort blame each other.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the Eastern Court has begun to regret its mistake and king and queen blame each other.

sentences.zh: 吾今還東，故遣告汝；

translations.literal: I now return east, therefore send word to tell you;
translations.idiomatic: I am heading east and send word;

sentences.zh: 吾已行矣，便可速發。」

translations.literal: I have already gone—you should set out at once."
translations.idiomatic: I am already on my way—leave at once."

sentences.zh: 令疑之，躊躇終日，又不可審覆。

translations.literal: Ling doubted it, hesitated all day, and could not verify it again.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ling suspected the message, wavered all day, and had no way to confirm it.

sentences.zh: 乃將舊騎，詐為出獵，遂奔樂安王臧於石門。

translations.literal: He then took his old mounted followers, pretended to go hunting, and fled to Prince of Le'an Zang at Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered his old retainers, feigned a hunting party, and fled to Prince of Le'an Murong Zang at Shimen.

sentences.zh: 猛表令叛狀，垂懼而出走，及藍田，為追騎所獲。

translations.literal: Meng memorialized Ling's rebellion; Chui was afraid and fled, and at Lantian was caught by pursuing horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng reported Ling's defection; Murong Chui fled in fear and was caught at Lantian by pursuers.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅引見東堂，勞之曰：「卿家國失和，委身投朕。

translations.literal: King of Qin Jian summoned him to audience in the Eastern Hall and comforted him, saying: "Your clan and state fell out; you entrusted yourself to us.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian received him in the Eastern Hall and said kindly, "Your house and state were at odds, and you came to me.

sentences.zh: 賢子心不忘本，猶懷首丘，亦各其志，不足深咎。

translations.literal: Your worthy son's heart does not forget its root; he still cherishes the homeward mound—each follows his will; it is not enough for deep blame.
translations.idiomatic: Your fine son still yearns for home—that is his nature, not a grave fault.

sentences.zh: 然燕之將亡，非令所能存，惜其徒入虎口耳。

translations.literal: Yet as Yan is about to perish, Ling cannot preserve it—I only regret that he rashly entered the tiger's maw.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yan is doomed and Ling cannot save it—I only pity him for leaping into the tiger's jaws.

sentences.zh: 且父子兄弟，罪不相及，卿何為過懼而狼狽如是乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover father and son, elder and younger brother—guilt does not extend to one another; why pass excessive fear and be so flustered as this!"
translations.idiomatic: Crimes do not pass from father to son—why panic and flee like this!"

sentences.zh: 待之如舊。

translations.literal: He treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: He treated Murong Chui as before.

sentences.zh: 燕人以令叛而復還，其父為秦所厚，疑令為反間，徙之沙城，在龍都東北六百裡。

translations.literal: The men of Yan, because Ling rebelled yet returned, and his father was treated generously by Qin, suspected Ling had been a double agent and moved him to Shacheng, six hundred li northeast of Longdu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan thought Murong Ling's defection and return, with his father favored by Qin, pointed to a double game, and exiled him to Shacheng, six hundred li northeast of the capital.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：昔周得微子而革商命，秦得由余而霸西戎，吳得伍員而克強楚，漢得陳平而誅項籍，魏得許攸而破袁紹。

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: In antiquity Zhou gained Weizi and changed Shang's mandate; Qin gained Youyu and hegemonized the Western Rong; Wu gained Wu Yuan and overcame mighty Chu; Han gained Chen Ping and executed Xiang Yu; Wei gained Xu You and broke Yuan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang remarks: Once Zhou won Weizi and overturned Shang; Qin won Youyu and ruled the western tribes; Wu won Wu Zixu and broke mighty Chu; Han won Chen Ping and destroyed Xiang Yu; Wei won Xu You and crushed Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 彼敵國之材臣，來為己用，進取之良資也。

translations.literal: Those talented ministers of enemy states who come to serve oneself are excellent capital for advance and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: Talented ministers from enemy states who enter one's service are assets for conquest.

sentences.zh: 王猛知慕容垂之心久而難信，獨不念燕尚未滅，垂以材高功盛，無罪見疑，窮困歸秦，未有異心，遽以猜忌殺之，是助燕為無道而塞來者之門也，如何其可哉！

translations.literal: Wang Meng knew Murong Chui's heart would in time be hard to trust, yet he alone did not consider that Yan was not yet destroyed—Chui, with talent high and achievement great, was suspected without guilt, came to Qin in distress, and had no alien mind—to kill him hastily out of suspicion would help Yan in its lack of the Way and block the gate for those who come; how could it be permissible!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng knew Murong Chui might never be fully trusted, yet forgot that Yan still stood—Murong Chui came in ruin, guilty of nothing, with no disloyal intent; to kill him from suspicion would justify Yan's wickedness and shut the door on future defectors. How could that be right!

sentences.zh: 故秦王堅禮以收燕望，親之以盡燕情，寵之以傾燕眾，信之以結燕心，未為過矣。

translations.literal: Therefore King of Qin Jian's using courtesy to win Yan's regard, intimacy to exhaust Yan's sentiment, favor to overturn Yan's masses, and trust to bind Yan's hearts was not excessive.
translations.idiomatic: So King Fu Jian's courtesy to win Yan's hope, intimacy to draw out Yan's loyalty, favor to sway Yan's people, and trust to bind Yan's hearts was no excess.

sentences.zh: 猛何汲汲於殺垂，至乃為市井鬻賣之行，有如嫉其寵而讒之者，豈雅德君子所宜為哉！

translations.literal: Why was Meng so eager to kill Chui—going so far as to conduct himself like a market hawker, as though one jealous of his favor were slandering him—is this what a gentleman of refined virtue ought to do!
translations.idiomatic: Why was Wang Meng so eager to kill Murong Chui that he stooped to street-market trickery, like a jealous rival whispering slander—what refined gentleman would do such a thing!

sentences.zh: 樂安王臧進屯滎陽，王猛遣建威將軍梁成、洛州刺史鄧羌擊走之；

translations.literal: Prince of Le'an Zang advanced and encamped at Xingyang; Wang Meng sent General Who Establishes Might Liang Cheng and Governor of Luo Province Deng Qiang to strike and drive him off;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Le'an Murong Zang advanced to Xingyang; Wang Meng sent Liang Cheng and Luo governor Deng Qiang to drive him back;

sentences.zh: 留羌鎮金墉，以輔國司馬桓寅為弘農太守，代羌戍陝城而還。

translations.literal: Deng Qiang was left to garrison Jinyong; Assistant State General of the Supporting Army Huan Yin was made Administrator of Hongnong to replace Qiang and garrison Shancheng, then Meng returned.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qiang held Jinyong; Huan Yin was made Hongnong administrator to replace him at Shancheng while Wang Meng withdrew.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅以王猛為司徒，錄尚書事，封平陽郡侯。

translations.literal: King of Qin Jian appointed Wang Meng as Minister over the Masses, recorder of the Masters of Writing, and ennobled him as Marquis of Pingyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian made Wang Meng Minister over the Masses and chief of the Secretariat, ennobling him as Marquis of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 猛固辭曰：「今燕、吳未平，戎車方駕，而始得一城，即受三事之賞，若克殄二寇，將何以加之！」

translations.literal: Meng firmly declined, saying: "Now Yan and Wu are not yet pacified, war chariots have just set forth, and having captured only one city you already grant the reward of the Three Offices—if the two enemies are exterminated, what can be added!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng firmly declined: "Yan and Wu remain unconquered, the armies have scarcely set out, and with one city taken you would already grant me the Three Highest Offices—what reward could you offer when both foes are destroyed?"

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「苟不暫抑朕心，何以顯卿謙光之美！

translations.literal: Jian said: "If I do not for a time restrain my heart, how shall your beauty of modest brilliance be displayed!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian replied, "Unless I briefly hold back my wishes, how can your virtue of humility shine forth?

sentences.zh: 已詔有司權聽所守；

translations.literal: I have already ordered the officials to allow temporarily what you hold to;
translations.idiomatic: I have directed the officials to let you retain your current posts for now;

sentences.zh: 封爵酬庸，其勉從朕命！」

translations.literal: ennoblement and fiefs reward merit—strive to follow my command!"
translations.idiomatic: accept rank and fief as reward for your service, and comply with my command!”

sentences.zh: 二月，癸酉，袁真卒。

translations.literal: In the second month, on guiyou, Yuan Zhen died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day guiyou, Yuan Zhen died.

sentences.zh: 陳郡太守朱輔立真子瑾為建威將軍，豫州刺史，以保壽春，遣其子乾之及司馬爨亮如鄴請命。

translations.literal: Chen Commandery Governor Zhu Fu installed Zhen's son Jin as General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Yu Province, to hold Shouchun; he sent his son Qianzhi and Clerk of the Army Cuan Liang to Ye to request orders.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fu, governor of Chen, made Yuan Zhen's son Yuan Jin General Who Establishes Might and inspector of Yu, to hold Shouchun, and sent his son Qianzhi and army clerk Cuan Liang to Ye for confirmation.

sentences.zh: 燕人以瑾為揚州刺史，輔為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: The Yan people appointed Jin Inspector of Yang Province and Fu Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yan recognized Jin as inspector of Yang and Fu as inspector of Jing.

sentences.zh: 三月，秦王堅以吏部尚書權翼為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the third month, King of Qin Jian appointed Ministry of Officials Chief Clerk Quan Yi as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, King Fu Jian made Quan Yi, chief clerk of the Ministry of Personnel, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，復以王猛為司徒，錄尚書事；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, he again appointed Wang Meng as Minister over the Masses and recorder of the Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, he again offered Wang Meng the posts of Minister over the Masses and chief secretary;

sentences.zh: 猛固辭，乃止。

translations.literal: Meng firmly declined, and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng again declined, and the offer was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 燕、秦皆遣兵助袁瑾，大司馬溫遣督護竺瑤等御之。

translations.literal: Both Yan and Qin sent troops to aid Yuan Jin; Grand Marshal Wen sent Superintendent Zhu Yao and others to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: Both Yan and Qin sent forces to aid Yuan Jin; Grand Marshal Huan Wen dispatched Zhu Yao and other commanders against them.

sentences.zh: 燕兵先至，瑤等與戰於武丘，破之。

translations.literal: Yan troops arrived first; Yao and others fought them at Wuqiu and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's army arrived first; Zhu Yao fought them at Wuqiu and routed them.

sentences.zh: 南頓太守桓石虔克其南城。

translations.literal: Nandun Governor Huan Shiqian captured their southern city.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Shiqian, governor of Nandun, took their southern citadel.

sentences.zh: 石虔，溫之弟子也。

translations.literal: Shiqian was Wen's younger brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Shiqian was a nephew of Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅復遣王猛督鎮南將軍楊安等十將步騎六萬以伐燕。

translations.literal: King of Qin Jian again sent Wang Meng to command ten generals including General Who Pacifies the South Yang An, with sixty thousand infantry and cavalry, to attack Yan.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian again dispatched Wang Meng at the head of ten generals, including Yang An, with sixty thousand troops to invade Yan.

sentences.zh: 慕容令自度終不得免，密謀起兵，沙城中謫戍士數千人，令皆厚撫之。

translations.literal: Murong Ling judged that in the end he could not escape, secretly plotted to raise troops; in Shazhong city several thousand garrison soldiers on penal service—Ling all treated them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ling knew he could not escape forever and secretly plotted rebellion; in Shazhong he won over thousands of exiled garrison troops with generous treatment.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚午，令殺牙門孟媯。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on gengwu, Ling killed Gate Commander Meng Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day gengwu, Murong Ling killed the gate commander Meng Wei.

sentences.zh: 城大涉圭懼，請自效。

translations.literal: City Commander Da Shegui was afraid and requested to prove himself by service.
translations.idiomatic: The city commander Da Shegui, fearing for his life, offered his services.

sentences.zh: 令信之，引置左右。

translations.literal: Ling trusted him and brought him close at hand.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ling believed him and kept him at his side.

sentences.zh: 遂帥謫戍士東襲威德城，殺城郎慕容倉，據城部署，遣人招東西諸戍，翕然皆應之。

translations.literal: He then led the penal garrison soldiers east to raid Weide city, killed City Officer Murong Cang, occupied the city and deployed forces, sent men to summon garrisons east and west—all responded with one accord.
translations.idiomatic: He then led the exiled garrison troops east to seize Weide, killed the commandant Murong Cang, organized the city's defenses, and sent envoys to garrisons east and west—all joined him at once.

sentences.zh: 鎮東將軍勃海王亮鎮龍城，令將襲之；

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the East, Prince of Bohai Liang, was stationed at Longcheng; Ling was about to attack it;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Bohai Murong Liang, general who pacified the east, held Longcheng; Murong Ling was preparing to attack it;

sentences.zh: 其弟麟以告亮，亮閉城拒守。

translations.literal: His younger brother Lin informed Liang; Liang closed the city and refused to yield.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Murong Lin warned Liang, who shut the gates and held firm.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，涉圭因侍直擊令，令單馬走，其黨皆潰。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Shegui, during attendance on duty, struck Ling; Ling fled alone on horseback, and his party all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Shegui seized his chance on guard duty and struck Murong Ling, who fled alone on horseback while his followers scattered.

sentences.zh: 涉圭追令至薛黎澤，擒而殺之，詣龍城白亮。

translations.literal: Shegui pursued Ling to Xueli Marsh, captured and killed him, then went to Longcheng to report to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Shegui pursued him to Xueli Marsh, captured and killed him, then went to Longcheng to report to Murong Liang.

sentences.zh: 亮為之誅涉圭，收令屍而葬之。

translations.literal: Liang for this executed Shegui, gathered Ling's corpse, and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had Shegui executed for the murder, recovered Murong Ling's body, and gave him burial.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙卯，秦王堅送王猛於灞上，曰：「今委卿以關東之任，當先破壺關，平上黨，長驅取鄴，所謂『疾雷不及掩耳』。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on yimao, King of Qin Jian escorted Wang Meng to Bashang and said: "Now I entrust you with the charge east of the Pass—you should first break Hukou Pass, pacify Shangdang, and drive straight to take Ye, as they say, 'Thunder so swift one cannot cover one's ears.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on yimao, King Fu Jian saw Wang Meng off at Bashang and said, "I entrust the eastern campaign to you—break Hukou, subdue Shangdang, and drive straight for Ye, as the saying goes, 'Lightning strikes before one can cover one's ears.

sentences.zh: 吾當親督萬眾，繼卿星發，舟車糧運，水陸俱進，卿勿以為後慮也。」

translations.literal: I shall personally command ten thousand masses, setting out in starry succession after you; boats and carts shall transport grain—land and water both advancing—you need not worry about support from behind."
translations.idiomatic: I will myself lead the main army in your wake; grain will move by land and water together—you need not fear being left without backup."

sentences.zh: 猛曰：「臣杖威靈，奉成算，蕩平殘胡，如風掃葉，願不煩鑾輿親犯塵霧，但願速敕所司部置鮮卑之所。」

translations.literal: Meng said: "Your servant, relying on Your Majesty's awesome spirit and carrying out the completed plan, will sweep away the remnant barbarians like wind scouring leaves. I wish only that the imperial carriage not trouble itself to face dust and mist—only that Your Majesty speedily order the officials to allot lands for the Xianbei."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng replied, "With Your Majesty's authority and a settled plan, I shall sweep the enemy aside like wind through leaves. I beg that you not ride forth into the dust yourself—only command officials promptly to settle the Xianbei wherever they are assigned."

sentences.zh: 堅大悅。

translations.literal: Jian was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸酉朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, first day guiyou, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the first day guiyou, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 秦王猛攻壺關，楊安攻晉陽。

translations.literal: King of Qin's Meng attacked Hukou Pass; Yang An attacked Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng attacked Hukou while Yang An besieged Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 八月，燕主暐命太傅上庸王評將中外精兵三十萬以拒秦。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Lord of Yan Wei ordered Grand Tutor Prince of Shangyong Ping to command three hundred thousand elite troops from within and without to resist Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Murong Wei ordered his grand tutor, Prince of Shangyong Murong Ping, to lead three hundred thousand picked troops against Qin.

sentences.zh: 暐以秦寇為憂，召散騎侍郎李鳳、黃門侍郎梁琛、中書侍郎樂嵩問曰：「秦兵眾寡何如？

translations.literal: Wei, worried about Qin raiders, summoned Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry Li Feng, Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Liang Chen, and Gentleman Attendant of the Central Secretariat Yue Song and asked: "Qin's soldiers—how are their numbers?
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei, anxious about the Qin invasion, summoned Li Feng, Liang Chen, and Yue Song and asked, "How numerous are Qin's forces?

sentences.zh: 今大軍既出，秦能戰乎？」

translations.literal: Now that the great army has set out, can Qin fight?"
translations.idiomatic: Now that our main army is in the field, will Qin dare to fight?

sentences.zh: 鳳曰：「秦國小兵弱，非王師之敵；

translations.literal: Feng said: "Qin is small, its soldiers weak—not a match for the royal army;
translations.idiomatic: Li Feng said, "Qin is small and its troops are weak—no match for our royal army;

sentences.zh: 景略常才，又非太傅之比，不足憂也。」

translations.literal: Jing Lue is ordinary talent, and again no comparison to the Grand Tutor—not worth worrying about."
translations.idiomatic: Jinglüe is merely ordinary talent, no match for the grand tutor—nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 琛、嵩曰：「勝敗在謀，不在眾寡。

translations.literal: Chen and Song said: "Victory and defeat lie in planning, not in many or few.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chen and Yue Song said, "Victory depends on strategy, not numbers.

sentences.zh: 秦遠來為寇，安肯不戰！

translations.literal: Qin coming from afar as invaders—how could they refuse to fight!
translations.idiomatic: Qin has marched from afar to invade—how could they refuse battle!

sentences.zh: 且吾當用謀以求勝，豈可冀其不戰而已乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover we should use stratagem to seek victory—how can we merely hope they will not fight!"
translations.idiomatic: We must win by strategy—can we simply hope they will not fight?

sentences.zh: 暐不悅。

translations.literal: Wei was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei was displeased.

sentences.zh: 王猛克壺關，執上黨太守南安王越，所過郡縣，皆望風降附，燕人大震。

translations.literal: Wang Meng captured Hukou Pass, seized Shangdang Governor Prince of Nan'an Yue; every commandery and county passed through submitted at the sight of his approach—the people of Yan were greatly shaken."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng took Hukou, captured Shangdang governor Prince of Nan'an Murong Yue, and everywhere he marched counties surrendered in dread—Yan was shaken."

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎封孚問司徒長史申胤曰：「事將何如？」

translations.literal: Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Feng Fu asked the Chancellor's Chief Clerk Shen Yin: "How will matters turn out?"
translations.idiomatic: Feng Fu, gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gate, asked Shen Yin, chief clerk to the chancellor, "How will this end?

sentences.zh: 胤歎曰：「鄴必亡矣，吾屬今茲將為秦虜。

translations.literal: Yin sighed and said: "Ye will surely fall; we of our sort this year will become Qin's captives.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yin sighed and said, "Ye will surely fall, and we shall become captives of Qin this year.

sentences.zh: 然越得歲而吳伐之，卒受其禍。

translations.literal: Yet Yue gained the year's advantage and Wu attacked it—in the end it suffered the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Yue had the year's luck and Wu attacked, Yue still met disaster in the end.

sentences.zh: 今福德在燕，秦雖得志，而燕之復建，不過一紀耳。」

translations.literal: Now fortune and virtue rest with Yan; though Qin may get its wish, Yan's restoration will be no more than one twelve-year cycle."
translations.idiomatic: Fortune now favors Yan; though Qin may prevail, Yan will rise again within twelve years.”

sentences.zh: 大司馬溫自廣陵帥眾二萬討袁瑾；

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Wen from Guangling led twenty thousand masses to attack Yuan Jin;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Huan Wen marched from Guangling with twenty thousand men against Yuan Jin;

sentences.zh: 以襄城太守劉波為淮南內史，將五千人鎮石頭。

translations.literal: He appointed Xiangcheng Governor Liu Bo as Interior Governor of Huainan, with five thousand men to garrison Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: He made Liu Bo, governor of Xiangcheng, interior governor of Huainan and stationed him at Shitou with five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 波，隗之孫也。

translations.literal: Bo was Kui's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bo was a grandson of Liu Kui.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，溫敗瑾於壽春，遂圍之。

translations.literal: On guichou, Wen defeated Jin at Shouchun and then besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Huan Wen defeated Yuan Jin at Shouchun and besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 燕左衛將軍孟高將騎兵救瑾，至淮北，未渡，會秦伐燕，燕召高還。

translations.literal: Yan's Left Guard General Meng Gao led cavalry to rescue Jin; reaching north of the Huai, before crossing, it happened that Qin attacked Yan, and Yan recalled Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's left guard general Meng Gao rode to Jin's aid but had reached only the north bank of the Huai when Qin invaded Yan and he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 廣漢妖賊李弘，詐稱漢歸義侯勢之子，聚眾萬餘人，自稱聖王，年號鳳凰。

translations.literal: Guanghan demonic bandit Li Hong falsely claimed to be son of Marquis Who Returns to Righteousness of Han Shi, gathered masses of more than ten thousand, styled himself Holy King, and established era name Fenghuang (Phoenix).
translations.idiomatic: In Guanghan, the rebel Li Hong claimed to be the son of Li Shi, Marquis Who Bends to Righteousness, rallied ten thousand followers, declared himself Holy King, and adopted the era name Phoenix.

sentences.zh: 隴西人李高，詐稱成主雄之子，攻破涪城，逐梁州刺史楊亮。

translations.literal: Longxi man Li Gao falsely claimed to be son of Lord of Cheng Xiong, broke Fucheng, and drove out Inspector of Liang Province Yang Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao of Longxi claimed to be a son of Li Xiong, seized Fucheng, and drove out Liang inspector Yang Liang.

sentences.zh: 九月，益州刺史周楚遣子瓊討高，又使瓊子梓潼太守颺討弘，皆平之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Inspector of Yi Province Zhou Chu sent his son Qiong to attack Gao, and also had Qiong's son, Zitong Governor Yang, attack Hong—all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Zhou Chu, inspector of Yi, sent his son Zhou Qiong against Li Gao and Zhou Qiong's son Yang, governor of Zitong, against Li Hong; both rebels were crushed.

sentences.zh: 秦楊安攻晉陽，晉陽兵多糧足，久之未下。

translations.literal: Qin's Yang An attacked Jinyang; Jinyang had many soldiers and ample grain—long time, not taken.
translations.idiomatic: Yang An of Qin besieged Jinyang, which was well-manned and well-supplied; the city held out for a long time.

sentences.zh: 王猛留屯騎校尉苟長戍壺關，引兵助安攻晉陽。

translations.literal: Wang Meng left Colonel of Garrison Cavalry Gou Chang to garrison Hukou Pass and led troops to assist An in attacking Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng left Gou Chang to hold Hukou and marched to help Yang An at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 為地道，使虎牙將軍張蚝帥壯士數百潛入城中，大呼斬關，納秦兵。

translations.literal: They dug an underground passage, had Tiger-tooth General Zhang Hao lead several hundred brave men to slip into the city, shout loudly and cut open the gate, and admit Qin troops.
translations.idiomatic: They dug a tunnel and sent Tiger-tooth General Zhang Hao with hundreds of picked warriors into the city; roaring, they cut down the gatekeepers and let the Qin army in.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，猛、安入晉陽，執燕并州刺史東海王莊。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Meng and An entered Jinyang and seized Yan's Inspector of Bing Province Prince of Donghai Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Wang Meng and Yang An entered Jinyang and captured Bing inspector Prince of Donghai Murong Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 太傅評畏猛，不敢進，屯於潞川。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Ping feared Meng, dared not advance, and encamped at Luchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Murong Ping, fearing Wang Meng, dared not advance and camped on the Luchuan.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛亥，猛留將軍武都毛當戍晉陽，進兵潞川，與慕容評相持。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on xinhai, Meng left General Wudu Mao Dang to garrison Jinyang, advanced to Luchuan, and faced off against Murong Ping.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on xinhai, Wang Meng left Mao Dang to hold Jinyang and marched to Luchuan to confront Murong Ping.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，猛遣將軍徐成覘燕軍形要，期以日中；

translations.literal: On renxu, Meng sent General Xu Cheng to reconnoiter the Yan army's formations and key points, with a deadline at noon;
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Wang Meng sent Xu Cheng to scout the Yan army's disposition, with orders to return by noon;

sentences.zh: 及昏而返，猛怒，將斬之。

translations.literal: when dusk came he returned; Meng was angry and was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: he did not return until dusk; Wang Meng flew into a rage and prepared to behead him.

sentences.zh: 鄧羌請之曰：「今賊眾我寡，詰朝將戰；

translations.literal: Deng Qiang pleaded for him, saying: "Now the enemy is many and we are few; tomorrow at dawn we will fight;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qiang pleaded for him: "The enemy outnumbers us, and we fight at dawn tomorrow;

sentences.zh: 成，大將也，宜且宥之。」

translations.literal: Cheng is a great general—it is fitting to pardon him for now."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Cheng is a senior commander—you should spare him for now.

sentences.zh: 猛曰：「若不殺成，軍法不立。」

translations.literal: Meng said: "If Cheng is not killed, military law will not stand."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng said, "If I spare Xu Cheng, military law means nothing.

sentences.zh: 羌固請曰：「成，羌之郡將也，雖違期應斬，羌願與成效戰以贖之。」

translations.literal: Qiang firmly pleaded: "Cheng is Qiang's district general; though missing the deadline he ought to be executed, Qiang wishes to fight together with Cheng in battle to redeem him."
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qiang pressed his case: "Cheng is my subordinate; though he deserves death for missing his deadline, I will fight at his side to redeem him."

sentences.zh: 猛弗許。

translations.literal: Meng did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng refused.

sentences.zh: 羌怒，還營，嚴鼓勒兵，將攻猛。

translations.literal: Qiang was angry, returned to camp, beat drums sternly and marshaled troops, preparing to attack Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Deng Qiang marched back to camp, sounding the drums and mustering his men to attack Wang Meng.

sentences.zh: 猛問其故，羌曰：「受詔討遠賊；

translations.literal: Meng asked the reason; Qiang said: "I received decree to attack distant enemies;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng asked why; Deng Qiang said, "I was ordered to fight distant enemies;

sentences.zh: 今有近賊，自相殺，欲先除之！」

translations.literal: now there are nearby enemies killing one another—I wish first to eliminate them!"
translations.idiomatic: now nearby enemies are killing each other—I mean to deal with them first!

sentences.zh: 猛謂羌義而有勇，使語之曰：「將軍止，吾今赦之。」

translations.literal: Meng judged Qiang righteous and brave, sent word to him: "General, stop—I now pardon him."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng saw both honor and courage in this, and sent word: "Stop, General—I pardon him now.

sentences.zh: 成既免，羌詣猛謝。

translations.literal: After Cheng was spared, Qiang went to Meng to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xu Cheng was spared, Deng Qiang came to Wang Meng to make amends.

sentences.zh: 猛執其手曰：「吾試將軍耳，將軍於郡將尚爾，況國家乎！

translations.literal: Meng took his hand and said: "I was testing the general; the general is like this toward a district general—how much more toward the state!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng grasped his hand and said, "I was testing you; if you show such loyalty to a subordinate, what will you do for the state!

sentences.zh: 吾不復憂賊矣！」

translations.literal: I need not again worry about the enemy!"
translations.idiomatic: I no longer fear the enemy!”

sentences.zh: 太傅評以猛懸軍深入，欲以持久制之。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Ping, because Meng's army hung suspended deep in advance, wished to use prolonged duration to control him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Murong Ping, seeing Wang Meng deep in hostile territory, planned to wear him down by attrition.

sentences.zh: 評為人貪鄙，鄣固山泉，鬻樵及水，積錢帛如丘陵；

translations.literal: Ping as a man was greedy and base—he blocked and fortified mountain springs, sold firewood and water, and amassed cash and silk like hills and mounds;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ping was greedy and mean; he sealed off mountain springs and sold firewood and water to his own troops, amassing coin and silk in heaps;

sentences.zh: 士卒怨憤，莫有鬥志。

translations.literal: soldiers resented and raged—none had fighting will.
translations.idiomatic: his soldiers grew bitter, and none had heart to fight.

sentences.zh: 猛聞之，笑曰：「慕容評真奴才，雖億兆之眾不足畏，況數十萬乎！

translations.literal: Meng heard it and laughed, saying: "Murong Ping is truly a slave-servant—even hundreds of millions would not be fearsome, let alone several hundred thousand!
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Meng heard this he laughed: "Murong Ping is a true slave-driver—even millions would not worry me, let alone a few hundred thousand!

sentences.zh: 吾今茲破之必矣。」

translations.literal: This time I shall break him—it is certain."
translations.idiomatic: I will crush him this time for certain.

sentences.zh: 乃遣游擊將軍郭慶帥騎五千，夜從間道出評營後，燒評輜重，火見鄴中。

translations.literal: He then sent Mobile General Guo Qing leading five thousand cavalry by night on a hidden route behind Ping's camp, burned Ping's baggage train—the fire was seen in Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Mobile General Guo Qing with five thousand horsemen by a secret night route behind Murong Ping's camp to burn his supply train; the flames were visible from Ye.

sentences.zh: 燕主暐懼，遣侍中蘭伊讓評曰：「王，高祖之子也，當以宗廟社稷為憂，奈何不撫戰士而榷賣樵水，專以貨殖為心乎！

translations.literal: Lord of Yan Wei was afraid, sent Palace Attendant Lan Yi to reprove Ping: "My lord, you are the son of the High Ancestor—you ought to take the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain as your worry; why not comfort the warriors but instead monopolize and sell firewood and water, making profit your sole heart!
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei, alarmed, sent Palace Attendant Lan Yi to rebuke Murong Ping: "You are a son of the founding emperor—you should worry for the altars of state; why do you neglect your soldiers and monopolize firewood and water for profit?

sentences.zh: 府庫之積，朕與王共之，何憂於貧！

translations.literal: The accumulations of the treasury—we share them, my lord and I—what worry about poverty!
translations.idiomatic: The treasury is yours as well as mine—what need to fear poverty!

sentences.zh: 若賊兵遂進，家國喪亡，王持錢帛欲安所置之！」

translations.literal: If the enemy troops then advance and family and state perish, my lord holding cash and silk—where would you place them!"
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy breaks through and the realm falls, where will you hoard your gold and silk then!

sentences.zh: 乃命悉以其錢帛散之軍士，且趨使戰。

translations.literal: He then ordered all the cash and silk to be distributed to the soldiers, and urged them to fight.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered all the hoarded wealth distributed to the troops and pressed Ping to give battle.

sentences.zh: 評大懼，遣使請戰於猛。

translations.literal: Ping was greatly afraid and sent envoys to request battle with Meng."
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Murong Ping sent envoys asking Wang Meng for battle."

sentences.zh: 甲子，猛陳於渭源而誓之曰：「王景略受國厚恩，任兼內外，今與諸君深入賊地，當竭力致死，有進無退，共立大功，以報國家。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Meng arrayed at Weiyuan and swore to them: "Wang Jing Lue has received the state's thick grace, his charge spanning inner and outer; now with you all I deep-enter enemy territory—we should exhaust strength unto death, advance without retreat, together establish great merit to repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Wang Meng drew up his army at Weiyuan and swore: "I, Wang Jinglüe, owe the state a great debt and hold power both at court and in the field; we march deep into enemy land—fight to the death, advance and never retreat, and together win glory for the realm.

sentences.zh: 受爵明君之朝，稱觴父母之室，不亦美乎！」

translations.literal: Receiving ennoblement in an enlightened lord's court, raising cups in the parents' chamber—is it not beautiful!"
translations.idiomatic: To receive honors in a wise ruler's court and toast your parents at home—what could be finer!

sentences.zh: 眾皆踴躍，破釜棄糧，大呼競進。

translations.literal: The masses all leaped eagerly, broke cauldrons and abandoned grain, shouted loudly and vied to advance."
translations.idiomatic: The troops shouted with zeal, smashed their pots and dropped their rations, and charged with a roar."

sentences.zh: 猛望燕兵之眾，謂鄧羌曰：「今日之事，非將軍不能破勍敵。

translations.literal: Meng looked at the Yan army's masses and said to Deng Qiang: "Today's affair—without the general we cannot break the strong enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing at the vast Yan host, Wang Meng told Deng Qiang, "Today's battle cannot be won without you.

sentences.zh: 成敗之機，在茲一舉，將軍勉之！」

translations.literal: The pivot of victory and defeat is in this one effort—the general, exert yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Everything hangs on this charge—do your utmost, General!

sentences.zh: 羌曰：「若能以司隸見與者，公勿以為憂。」

translations.literal: Qiang said: "If the Inspectorate of the Capital Metropolis can be given to me, my lord need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qiang replied, "Grant me the post of metropolitan inspector, and you need not worry."

sentences.zh: 猛曰：「此非吾所及也，必以安定太守、萬戶侯相處。」

translations.literal: Meng said: "This is not within my reach—it must be that I treat you as Governor of Anding and a marquis of ten thousand households."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng said, "That is beyond my power—I can only offer you the governorship of Anding and a marquisate of ten thousand households."

sentences.zh: 羌不悅而退。

translations.literal: Qiang unhappily withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Displeased, Deng Qiang withdrew.

sentences.zh: 俄而兵交，猛召羌，羌寢弗應。

translations.literal: Soon the armies clashed; Meng summoned Qiang—Qiang lay abed and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Battle joined; Wang Meng called for Deng Qiang, who stayed in his tent and would not answer.

sentences.zh: 猛馳就許之，羌乃大飲帳中，與張蚝、徐成等跨馬運矛，馳赴燕陳；

translations.literal: Meng galloped to him and promised it; Qiang then drank heavily in the tent, and with Zhang Hao, Xu Cheng, and others mounted horses wielding spears and galloped toward the Yan formation;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng rode to him in person and granted his request; Deng Qiang then drank deep in his tent, and with Zhang Hao, Xu Cheng, and others mounted, wheeled their spears, and charged the Yan lines;

sentences.zh: 出入數四，旁若無人，所殺傷數百。

translations.literal: entering and exiting several times four, as if no one were beside them—those killed and wounded numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: they rode in and out four times as though no one else were on the field, killing and wounding hundreds.

sentences.zh: 及日中，燕兵大敗，俘斬五萬餘人，乘勝追擊，所殺及降者又十萬餘人，評單騎走還鄴。

translations.literal: By midday the Yan army was greatly defeated—more than fifty thousand captured and beheaded; riding victory in pursuit, those killed and those who surrendered totaled another hundred thousand and more—Ping fled alone on horseback back to Ye."
translations.idiomatic: By noon the Yan army lay in ruins: more than fifty thousand killed or captured; in the pursuit another hundred thousand fell or surrendered, and Murong Ping fled alone on horseback back to Ye."

sentences.zh: 崔鴻曰：鄧羌請郡將以撓法，徇私也；

translations.literal: Cui Hong said: Deng Qiang requested the commandery general to bend the law—this was favoring private interest;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong commented: In asking the provincial commander to set aside military law, Deng Qiang was putting private interest first;

sentences.zh: 勒兵欲攻王猛，無上也；

translations.literal: marshaling troops intending to attack Wang Meng—there is none more insubordinate;
translations.idiomatic: in drawing up his soldiers to attack Wang Meng he reached the height of insubordination;

sentences.zh: 臨戰豫求司隸，邀君也。

translations.literal: on the eve of battle beforehand seeking the post of Director of Retainers—this was coercing his lord.
translations.idiomatic: and in demanding the post of Metropolitan Commandant on the eve of battle he was holding his sovereign to ransom.

sentences.zh: 有此三者，罪孰大焉！

translations.literal: having these three things, what crime could be greater!
translations.idiomatic: Given these three offenses, which crime could rank above them?

sentences.zh: 猛能容其所短，收其所長，若馴猛虎，馭悍馬，以成大功。

translations.literal: Meng could tolerate his shortcomings and gather in his strengths—like taming a fierce tiger, driving an unruly horse—to complete great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wang Meng overlooked his faults and put his strengths to use, as one tames a savage tiger or rides a spirited horse, and so won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 《詩》雲：「采葑采菲，無以下體。」

translations.literal: The Odes say: "Gather turnips, gather radishes—do not reject them for the lower part."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Songs says: "We gather turnips, we gather radishes; do not reject them for what lies below."

sentences.zh: 猛之謂矣。

translations.literal: Such applies to Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Such was Wang Meng's way.

sentences.zh: 秦兵長驅而東，丁卯，圍鄴。

translations.literal: Qin troops drove straight east; on dingmao they besieged Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin army swept eastward; on dingmao it encircled Ye.

sentences.zh: 猛上疏稱：「臣以甲子之日，大殲丑類。

translations.literal: Meng submitted a memorial stating: "Your servant on the day jiazi greatly annihilated the wicked kind.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng memorialized the throne: "On the day jiazi your servant annihilated the enemy host.

sentences.zh: 順陛下仁愛之志，使六州士庶，不覺易主，自非守迷違命，一無所害。」

translations.literal: Following Your Majesty's humane and loving intent, causing the gentry and commoners of six provinces not to feel the change of ruler—except those who hold fast to delusion and disobey orders, none are harmed."
translations.idiomatic: In accord with Your Majesty's merciful purpose I have let the people of six provinces scarcely feel that their ruler has changed; save those who stubbornly resist, none have come to harm.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅報之曰：「將軍役不逾時，而元惡克舉，勳高前古。

translations.literal: Emperor Fu Jian of Qin replied: "General, the campaign did not exceed its season, yet the arch-villain was taken—merit surpassing antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Fu Jian replied: "General, you finished within the allotted time and destroyed the chief foe—achievement higher than any in olden days.

sentences.zh: 朕今親帥六軍，星言電赴。

translations.literal: I now personally lead the six armies, stars speaking, lightning hurrying.
translations.idiomatic: I now lead the imperial host myself, marching as swiftly as a shooting star.

sentences.zh: 將軍其休養將士，以待朕至，然後取之。」

translations.literal: General, rest and recuperate officers and soldiers, wait until I arrive, then take it."
translations.idiomatic: Rest your men and wait for my arrival before you deliver the final stroke.”

sentences.zh: 猛之未至也，鄴帝剽劫公行，及猛至，遠近貼然。

translations.literal: Before Meng's arrival, robbers plundered on the public roads at Ye; when Meng arrived, near and far were settled calm.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wang Meng arrived, bandits roamed the roads around Ye; once he came, peace returned far and near.

sentences.zh: 號令嚴明，軍無私犯，法簡政寬，燕民各安其業，更相謂曰：「不圖今日復見太原王！」

translations.literal: Orders and commands were strict and clear; the army made no private violations; laws were simple, government lenient—the people of Yan each rested in their occupations, saying to one another: "We never expected today again to see the Prince of Taiyuan!"
translations.idiomatic: His discipline was iron, his soldiers scrupulous, his laws light and his rule gentle; the people of Yan went safely about their trades and said to one another, "We never thought we would see the Prince of Taiyuan's ways again!

sentences.zh: 猛聞之，歎曰：「慕容玄恭信奇士也，可謂古之遺愛矣！」

translations.literal: Meng heard it and sighed: "Murong Xuangong was truly an extraordinary man—one may call him a legacy of ancient loving kindness!"
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Meng heard this he sighed: "Murong Xuangong was indeed a rare man—his kindness still reaches us from ages past!

sentences.zh: 設太牢以祭之。

translations.literal: He set out the grand offering to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: He offered the highest sacrificial rites in Murong Jun's honor.

sentences.zh: 十一月，秦王堅留李威輔太子守長安，陽平公融鎮洛陽，自帥精銳十萬赴鄴，七日而至安陽，宴祖父時故老。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Emperor Fu Jian of Qin left Li Wei to assist the crown prince in guarding Chang'an, Yangping Duke Fu Rong to hold Luoyang, and personally led one hundred thousand picked troops toward Ye—seven days later reaching Anyang, feasting the old elders from his grandfather's time.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Fu Jian left Li Wei to help the crown prince guard Chang'an and Yangping Duke Fu Rong to hold Luoyang, then marched east with a hundred thousand elite troops; in seven days he reached Anyang and banqueted the elders who had known his grandfather.

sentences.zh: 猛潛如安陽謁堅，堅曰：「昔周亞夫不迎漢文帝，今將軍臨敵而棄軍，何也？」

translations.literal: Meng secretly went to Anyang to visit Fu Jian; Fu Jian said: "Formerly Zhou Yafu did not welcome Emperor Wen of Han—now the general abandons the army facing the enemy; why?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng slipped away to Anyang to see Fu Jian, who said: "Long ago Zhou Yafu would not receive Emperor Wen of Han at his camp—now you leave the field while the enemy is still before you. Why?

sentences.zh: 猛曰：「亞夫前卻人主以求名，臣竊少之。

translations.literal: Meng said: "Yafu formerly pushed back his sovereign to seek reputation—your servant privately holds this in slight esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng answered: "Yafu turned his emperor away to win a reputation for strictness—I have never admired that.

sentences.zh: 且臣奉陛下威靈，擊垂亡之虜，譬如釜中之魚，何足慮也！

translations.literal: Moreover your servant bears Your Majesty's awesome spirit, striking foes on the verge of death—like fish in a cauldron; what need for worry!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, under Your Majesty's majesty I strike a doomed foe—fish in a boiling pot. What is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 監國沖幼，鸞駕遠臨，脫有不虞，悔之何及！

translations.literal: The regent Chong is young; the imperial carriage comes from afar—if unexpectedly something untoward occurs, regret would never catch up!
translations.idiomatic: The regent Fu Chong is still a boy, and you would ride far from the capital—if misfortune should come, regret would come too late!

sentences.zh: 陛下忘臣灞上之言邪！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has forgotten your servant's words at Bashang!"
translations.idiomatic: Has Your Majesty forgotten what I told you at Bashang?”

sentences.zh: 初，燕宜都王桓帥眾萬餘屯沙亭，為太傅評後繼，聞評敗，引兵屯內黃。

translations.literal: Initially, Murong Huan, Prince of Yidu of Yan, leading more than ten thousand men encamped at Shating as Grand Tutor Ping's rear support; hearing of Ping's defeat, he led troops to encamp at Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Murong Huan, Prince of Yidu, had camped at Shating with ten thousand men as Murong Ping's reserve; when Ping was defeated he withdrew to Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 堅使鄧羌攻信都。

translations.literal: Fu Jian sent Deng Qiang to attack Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian dispatched Deng Qiang against Xindu.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，桓帥鮮卑五千奔龍城。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Huan led five thousand Xianbei fleeing to Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Murong Huan fled to Longcheng with five thousand Xianbei horsemen.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，燕散騎侍郎餘蔚帥扶餘、高句麗及上黨質子五百餘人，夜，開鄴北門，納秦兵，燕主暐與上庸王評、樂安王臧、字襄王淵、左衛將軍孟高、殿中將軍艾朗等奔龍城。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Yan's Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Yu Wei led Fuyu, Goguryeo, and more than five hundred hostages from Shangdang; at night they opened Ye's north gate and admitted Qin troops; Lord of Yan Wei with Prince of Shangyong Ping, Prince of Le'an Zang, Prince Zixiang Yuan, Left Guard General Meng Gao, Palace Guard General Ai Lang, and others fled to Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Yu Wei, a Yan chamberlain, opened Ye's north gate by night with five hundred Fuyu, Goguryeo, and Shangdang hostages and let the Qin army in; Murong Wei fled to Longcheng with Murong Ping, Le'an Prince Murong Zang, Beixiang Prince Murong Yuan, Meng Gao, Ai Lang, and others.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，秦王堅入鄴宮。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Emperor Fu Jian of Qin entered Ye Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Fu Jian entered the palace at Ye.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂見燕公卿大夫及故時僚吏，有慍色。

translations.literal: Murong Chui saw Yan's dukes, ministers, grandees, and former time subordinate officials—with angry color.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Chui met Yan's former ministers and officials, his face showed anger.

sentences.zh: 高弼言於垂曰：「大王憑祖宗積累之資，負英傑高世之略，遭值迍阨，棲集外邦。

translations.literal: Gao Bi spoke to Chui: "Great King relies on accumulated resources of ancestors and bears heroic surpassing-the-age strategy—encountering obstruction and peril, nesting and gathering in a foreign state.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Bi said to him: "Your Highness draws on the accumulated strength of your house and on gifts that set you above your age; you have suffered ruin and dwell now in a foreign land.

sentences.zh: 今雖家國傾覆，安知其不為興運之始邪！

translations.literal: Now though family and state have toppled—who knows it may not be the start of rising fortune!
translations.idiomatic: Though our state has fallen, who knows but this is the seed of a new rise?

sentences.zh: 愚謂國之舊人，宜恢江海之量，有以慰結其心，以立覆簣之基，成九仞之功，奈何以一怒捐之？

translations.literal: This fool considers the state's old people—one should expand the measure of rivers and seas, have means to comfort and bind their hearts, to establish the foundation of a basket of earth overturned, complete the nine ren of merit—how can one throw them away in a single rage?
translations.idiomatic: Your old countrymen should be met with the breadth of river and sea; win their hearts and you lay the first basket of earth for a nine-fathom tower—why cast that away in a moment's wrath?

sentences.zh: 愚竊為大王不取也！」

translations.literal: This fool privately considers it something the Great King ought not take!"
translations.idiomatic: I must say, my lord, that would be unwise.

sentences.zh: 垂悅，從之。

translations.literal: Chui was pleased and followed it."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui took the advice and did as he was urged."

sentences.zh: 燕主暐之出鄴也，衛士猶千餘騎，既出城，皆散，惟十餘騎從行；

translations.literal: When Lord of Yan Wei left Ye, guard soldiers still numbered more than a thousand riders; once out of the city, all dispersed—only ten-plus riders followed;
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Wei fled Ye he still had a thousand guards, but once outside the walls they all scattered and only a dozen horsemen rode with him;

sentences.zh: 秦王堅使游擊將軍郭慶追之。

translations.literal: Emperor Fu Jian of Qin sent Mobile General Guo Qing to pursue him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent Mobile General Guo Qing in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 時道路艱難，孟高扶侍暐，經護二王，極其勤瘁，又所在遇盜，轉斗而前。

translations.literal: At the time roads were difficult; Meng Gao supported and served Wei, carefully guarding the two princes, to the utmost of weary toil; moreover wherever they went they met bandits, fighting turn by turn as they advanced.
translations.idiomatic: The roads were treacherous; Meng Gao attended Murong Wei and guarded the two princes with tireless devotion, fighting bandits at every turn as they pressed forward.

sentences.zh: 數日，行至福祿，依塚解息，盜二十餘人猝至，皆挾弓矢，高持刀與戰，殺傷數人。

translations.literal: Several days later, reaching Fulu, they rested by a mound; more than twenty bandits suddenly arrived, all bearing bows and arrows; Gao took knife and fought, killing and wounding several men.
translations.idiomatic: After several days they reached Fulu and rested by a tomb; more than twenty armed bandits fell upon them, and Meng Gao fought with his blade, killing or wounding several.

sentences.zh: 高力極，自度必死，乃直前抱一賊，頓擊於地，大呼曰：「男兒窮矣！」

translations.literal: Gao's strength reached its limit; he reckoned he must die, then went straight forward, embraced one bandit, slammed him striking to the ground, loudly shouting: "A man has come to his end!"
translations.idiomatic: Exhausted and knowing he would die, he seized one robber, dashed him to the ground, and cried out: "This is as far as a man can go!

sentences.zh: 餘賊從帝射高，殺之。

translations.literal: The remaining bandits, in the emperor's presence, shot at Gao and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining bandits shot at him before Murong Wei and killed him.

sentences.zh: 艾朗見高獨戰，亦還趨賊，並死。

translations.literal: Ai Lang saw Gao fighting alone, also turned back rushing at bandits—both died together.
translations.idiomatic: Ai Lang saw Meng Gao fighting alone, wheeled back toward the bandits, and died beside him.

sentences.zh: 暐失馬步走，郭慶追及於高陽，部將巨武將縛之，暐曰：「汝何小人，敢縛天子！」

translations.literal: Wei lost his horse and went on foot; Guo Qing caught up at Gaoyang; subordinate general Ju Wu was about to bind him; Wei said: "You—what petty man—dares bind the Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei lost his horse and fled on foot until Guo Qing caught him at Gaoyang; as the subordinate Ju Wu moved to bind him, Wei cried: "How dare a wretch like you bind the Son of Heaven!

sentences.zh: 武曰：「我受詔追賊，何謂天子！」

translations.literal: Wu said: "I receive the edict to pursue the bandit—what is called Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Ju Wu replied: "I follow an order to seize a fugitive—what Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 執以詣秦王堅。

translations.literal: He seized him and took him before Emperor Fu Jian of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He bound Murong Wei and brought him before Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 堅詰其不降而走之狀，對曰：「狐死首丘，欲歸死於先人墳墓耳。」

translations.literal: Fu Jian interrogated him on his condition of not surrendering but fleeing; he replied: "When the fox dies its head faces the mound—I wished to return and die at my ancestors' graves, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian asked why he had refused surrender and fled; Murong Wei answered: "When a fox dies its head turns homeward—I wished only to die among my forefathers' graves.

sentences.zh: 堅哀而釋之，令還宮，帥文武出降。

translations.literal: Fu Jian pitied him and released him, ordered him to return to the palace, leading civil and military to come out and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Fu Jian freed him and sent him back to the palace to lead his ministers out in formal surrender.

sentences.zh: 暐稱孟高、艾朗之忠於堅，堅命厚加斂葬，拜其子為郎中。

translations.literal: Wei praised Meng Gao and Ai Lang's loyalty to Fu Jian; Fu Jian ordered richly to bury them and appointed their sons as Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei commended Meng Gao and Ai Lang's loyalty; Fu Jian had them buried with honor and made their sons palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 郭慶進至龍城，太傅評奔高句麗，高句麗執評，送於秦。

translations.literal: Guo Qing advanced to Longcheng; Grand Tutor Ping fled to Goguryeo; Goguryeo seized Ping and delivered him to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qing pressed on to Longcheng; Murong Ping fled to Goguryeo, which captured him and sent him to Qin.

sentences.zh: 宜都王桓殺鎮東將軍勃海王亮，並其眾，奔遼東。

translations.literal: Prince of Yidu Huan killed Eastern Pacifying General Prince of Bohai Liang, united his forces, and fled to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huan murdered Eastern Pacifying General Prince Murong Liang of Bohai, absorbed his troops, and fled to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 遼東太守韓稠，先已降秦，桓至，不得入，攻之，不克。

translations.literal: Liaodong Administrator Han Chou had already surrendered to Qin first; when Huan arrived he could not enter, attacked, and did not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong governor Han Chou had already submitted to Qin; Murong Huan could not enter, besieged him, and failed.

sentences.zh: 郭慶遣將軍朱嶷擊之，桓充眾單走，嶷獲而殺之。

translations.literal: Guo Qing sent General Zhu Ni to attack him; Huan with full host fled alone; Ni captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qing sent General Zhu Ni against him; Murong Huan abandoned his army and fled alone; Zhu Ni captured and executed him.

sentences.zh: 諸州牧守及六夷渠帥盡降於秦，凡得郡百五十七，戶二百四十六萬，口九百九十九萬。

translations.literal: All provincial governors and guardians and the six barbarian channel chiefs completely surrendered to Qin—in all obtaining one hundred fifty-seven commanderies, two million four hundred sixty thousand households, nine million nine hundred ninety thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Every provincial governor and tribal chief submitted to Qin; in all he gained one hundred fifty-seven commanderies, 2.46 million households, and 9.99 million people.

sentences.zh: 以燕宮人、珍寶分賜將士。

translations.literal: With Yan palace women and precious treasures he distributed bestowing on officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He divided Yan's palace women and treasures among his officers and men.

sentences.zh: 下詔大赦曰：「朕以寡薄，猥承休命，不能懷遠以德，柔服四維，至使戎車屢駕，有害斯民，雖百姓之過，然亦朕之罪也。

translations.literal: He issued an edict of great amnesty saying: "I with meager thinness rashly received the beautiful mandate; could not cherish the distant through virtue, gently subdue the four corners—so that war chariots repeatedly were driven, harming these people; though the common people's fault, yet also my crime.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty: "My virtues are few, yet I rashly received the mandate; I failed to win the far reaches through kindness or to soften the realm in all directions, so that chariots of war went forth again and again to the harm of the people. The fault lies with the people, but the blame is mine as well.

sentences.zh: 其大赦天下，與之更始。」

translations.literal: Let there be great amnesty under Heaven, with them beginning anew."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore let the empire be pardoned and begin anew with a clean slate.”

sentences.zh: 初，梁琛之使秦也，以侍輦苟純為副。

translations.literal: Initially, when Liang Chen was envoy to Qin, he took Palace Escort Gou Chun as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Chen first went as envoy to Qin, Gou Chun served as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 琛每應對，不先告純；

translations.literal: Chen each time in responding did not first inform Chun;
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chen answered every question without consulting Gou Chun beforehand;

sentences.zh: 純恨之，歸，言於燕主暐曰：「琛在長安，與王猛甚親善，疑有異謀。」

translations.literal: Chun resented this; returned, spoke to Lord of Yan Wei: "Chen in Chang'an was very close and friendly with Wang Meng—suspected of having a separate plot."
translations.idiomatic: Gou Chun hated this; back in Yan he told Murong Wei: "In Chang'an Liang Chen grew very close to Wang Meng—I suspect treachery.

sentences.zh: 琛又數稱秦王堅及王猛之美，且言秦將興師，宜為之備。

translations.literal: Chen also repeatedly praised the excellence of Emperor Fu Jian of Qin and Wang Meng, and added Qin would raise armies—one ought to prepare against it.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chen also praised Fu Jian and Wang Meng openly and warned that Qin would invade—Yan should prepare.

sentences.zh: 已而秦果伐燕，皆如琛言，暐乃疑琛知其情。

translations.literal: Soon after Qin indeed attacked Yan—all as Chen had said; Wei then suspected Chen knew their plans.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin attacked exactly as Liang Chen had foretold, Murong Wei began to suspect he had known more than he let on.

sentences.zh: 及慕容評敗，遂收琛繫獄。

translations.literal: When Murong Ping was defeated, he then seized Chen and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: After Murong Ping's defeat he threw Liang Chen in prison.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅入鄴而釋之，除中書著作郎，引見，謂之曰：「卿昔言上庸王、吳王皆將相奇材，何為不能謀畫，自使亡國？」

translations.literal: When Emperor Fu Jian of Qin entered Ye he released him, appointed him Secretariat Compiler, summoned and saw him, said to him: "You formerly said Prince of Shangyong and Prince of Wu were both minister-general marvelous material—why could they not scheme and plan, causing their own state to perish?"
translations.idiomatic: After taking Ye Fu Jian freed him, made him a compiler in the secretariat, and asked: "You once praised the Prince of Shangyong and the Prince of Wu as rare talent in statecraft—why could they not save their country from ruin?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「天命廢興，豈二人所能移也！」

translations.literal: He replied: "Heaven's mandate's abandonment and rise—how could two men shift it!"
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chen answered: "The rise and fall of dynasties is Heaven's decree—how could two men overturn it?

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「卿不能見幾而作，虛稱燕美，忠不自防，返為身禍，可謂智乎？」

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "You could not see the subtle sign and act—falsely praised Yan's beauty, loyalty without self-protection, in return becoming personal disaster—can this be called wisdom?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said: "You failed to read the signs in time, praised Yan without cause, kept faith without guarding yourself, and brought ruin on your own head—is that wisdom?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣聞『幾者動之微，吉兇之先見者也。』

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant hears: 'The subtle is the faintness of movement—the first appearance of fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "I have heard that 'the subtle' is the first tremor of events, the foreshadowing of fortune or doom.

sentences.zh: 如臣愚闇，實所不及。

translations.literal: Such as your servant's stupidity and darkness—truly what is not reached.
translations.idiomatic: In my dullness I could never grasp such things.

sentences.zh: 然為臣莫如忠，為子莫如孝，自非有一至之心者，莫能保忠孝之始終。

translations.literal: Yet in being minister nothing surpasses loyalty; in being son nothing surpasses filial piety—unless one has a single utmost heart, none can preserve loyalty and filial piety from start to finish.
translations.idiomatic: Yet nothing becomes a minister like loyalty, or a son like filial piety; only one utterly devoted can carry duty and devotion from first to last.

sentences.zh: 是以古之烈士，臨危不改，見死不避，以徇君親。

translations.literal: Therefore the heroic martyrs of old, facing peril did not change, seeing death did not avoid—to follow with body for lord and parent.
translations.idiomatic: That is why heroes of old faced danger unflinching and death unafraid for sovereign and kin.

sentences.zh: 彼知幾者，心達安危，身擇去就，不顧家國，臣就使知之，尚不忍為，況非所及邪！」

translations.literal: Those who know the subtle—their hearts penetrate safety and peril, their bodies choose going and staying, not caring for family and state; your servant even if made to know would still not bear to do it—how much less what is not reached!"
translations.idiomatic: Those who read the signs choose safety over peril, pick their moment and think nothing of country or kin; even if I had such knowledge I would still refuse to act on it—much less attain it!”

sentences.zh: 堅聞悅綰之忠，恨不及見，拜其子為郎中。

translations.literal: Fu Jian heard of Yue Wan's loyalty, regretted not reaching in time to see him, appointed his son as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian heard of Yue Wan's faithful death and, grieving that he could not meet him, made Yue Wan's son a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 堅以王猛為使持節、都督關東六州諸軍事、車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、冀州牧，鎮鄴，進爵清河郡侯，悉以慕容評第中之物賜之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian made Wang Meng Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander of all military affairs of the six eastern provinces east of the Pass, Chariot-and-Cavalry Grand General, Grand Master with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, Governor of Ji Province, stationed at Ye, advanced in nobility to Marquis of Qinghe Commandery—all items within Murong Ping's mansion given to him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian made Wang Meng commander of the six eastern provinces with full military authority, Chariot-and-Cavalry Grand General, and Governor of Ji, stationed at Ye as Marquis of Qinghe, and gave him everything in Murong Ping's mansion.

sentences.zh: 賜楊安爵博平縣侯；

translations.literal: Bestowed Yang An the nobility of Marquis of Boxian County;
translations.idiomatic: Yang An was created Marquis of Boxian;

sentences.zh: 以鄧羌為使持節、征虜將軍、安定太守，賜爵真定郡侯；

translations.literal: Made Deng Qiang Bearer of the Staff, General Who Conquers Barbarians, Administrator of Anding, bestowed nobility Marquis of Zhending Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qiang was made Bearer of the Staff, General Who Conquers Barbarians, and Administrator of Anding, with the title Marquis of Zhending;

sentences.zh: 郭慶為持節、都督幽州諸軍事、幽州刺史，鎮薊，賜爵襄城侯。

translations.literal: Guo Qing as Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs of You Province, Governor of You, stationed at Ji, bestowed nobility Marquis of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qing was made governor and military commander of You Province, stationed at Ji as Marquis of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 其餘將士封賞各有差。

translations.literal: The remaining officers and soldiers—enfeoffment and reward each had difference.
translations.idiomatic: Other officers and men were rewarded according to their merit.

sentences.zh: 堅以京兆韋鐘為魏郡太守，彭豹為陽平太守；

translations.literal: Fu Jian made Jingzhao Wei Zhong Administrator of Wei Commandery, Peng Bao Administrator of Yangping;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian appointed Wei Zhong of Jingzhao governor of Wei Commandery and Peng Bao governor of Yangping;

sentences.zh: 其餘州縣牧、守、令、長，皆因舊而授之。

translations.literal: The remaining provinces, counties—governors, guardians, magistrates, chiefs—all followed the old in appointing them.
translations.idiomatic: For the rest he kept the existing prefects, governors, and magistrates in post.

sentences.zh: 以燕常山太守申紹為散騎侍郎，使與散騎侍郎京兆韋儒俱為繡衣使者，循行關東州郡，觀省風俗，勸課農桑，振恤窮困，收葬死亡，旌顯節行，燕政有不便於民者，皆變除之。

translations.literal: Made Yan's Changshan Administrator Shen Shao Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, sent him with Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Jingzhao Wei Ru both as Embroidered-Robe Envoys, circulating through eastern provinces and commanderies, observing and inspecting customs, urging and surveying agriculture and sericulture, relieving and succoring the poor and distressed, collecting and burying the dead, displaying and making manifest upright conduct—all Yan policies not convenient for the people, all changed and removed.
translations.idiomatic: He made Shen Shao and Wei Ru embroidered-robes inspectors to tour the eastern provinces, review local customs, promote farming, aid the poor, bury the dead with honor, and reward virtue; every Yan regulation that harmed the people was abolished.

sentences.zh: 十二月，秦王堅遷慕容暐及燕後妃、王公、百官並鮮卑四萬餘戶於長安。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Emperor Fu Jian of Qin transferred Murong Wei and Yan's empresses, princes and dukes, hundred officials, together with more than forty thousand Xianbei households to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Fu Jian moved Murong Wei, the Yan royal household, the nobles and officials, and more than forty thousand Xianbei families to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 王猛表留梁琛為主簿，領記室督。

translations.literal: Wang Meng memorialized to retain Liang Chen as Chief Clerk, leading the secretariat director.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng asked to keep Liang Chen as his chief clerk and head of his secretariat.

sentences.zh: 它日，猛與僚屬宴，語及燕朝使者，猛曰：「人心不同。

translations.literal: Another day, Meng feasted with subordinate officials; speech reached Yan court envoys; Meng said: "Human hearts are not the same.
translations.idiomatic: One evening at a feast with his staff Wang Meng spoke of the Yan envoys and said: "Men's hearts differ.

sentences.zh: 昔梁君至長安，專美本朝；

translations.literal: Formerly Lord Liang reached Chang'an, exclusively praised this court;
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chen came to Chang'an and would speak only of Yan's virtues;

sentences.zh: 樂君但言桓溫軍盛；

translations.literal: Lord Yue only spoke of Huan Wen's armies flourishing;
translations.idiomatic: Yue spoke of nothing but Huan Wen's strength;

sentences.zh: 郝君微說國弊。」

translations.literal: Lord Hao slightly spoke of the state's decay."
translations.idiomatic: Hao barely hinted at Yan's weakness.

sentences.zh: 參軍馮誕曰：「今三子皆為國臣，敢問取臣之道何先？」

translations.literal: Staff Officer Feng Yan said: "Now the three gentlemen are all state ministers—dare I ask: in taking ministers, what comes first?"
translations.idiomatic: His aide Feng Yan asked: "All three now serve your lordship—which quality matters most in choosing a minister?

sentences.zh: 猛曰：「郝君知幾為先。」

translations.literal: Meng said: "Lord Hao's knowing the subtle comes first."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng said: "Hao's gift for reading the signs comes first."

sentences.zh: 誕曰：「然則明公賞丁公而誅季布也。」

translations.literal: Yan said: "Then the enlightened lord rewards Duke Ding and executes Ji Bu."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yan said: "Then you would reward the turncoat and execute the faithful man."

sentences.zh: 猛大笑。

translations.literal: Meng laughed greatly."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng laughed heartily."

sentences.zh: 秦王堅自鄴如枋頭，宴父老，改枋頭為永昌，復之終世。

translations.literal: Emperor Fu Jian of Qin from Ye went to Fangtou, feasted the elders, changed Fangtou to Yongchang, exempted it for life.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian went from Ye to Fangtou, feasted the local elders, renamed the place Yongchang, and exempted it from taxes for life.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，至長安，封慕容暐為新興侯；

translations.literal: On jiayin, reached Chang'an; enfeoffed Murong Wei as Marquis of Xinxing;
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin he reached Chang'an and created Murong Wei Marquis of Xinxing;

sentences.zh: 以燕故臣慕容評為給事中，皇甫真為奉車都尉，李洪為駙馬都尉，皆奉朝請。

translations.literal: Made Yan's former ministers Murong Ping Masters of Writing, Huangfu Zhen Commandant of the Court Carriages, Li Hong Commandant of the Horse Caparison—all Attendants at Court.
translations.idiomatic: Former Yan ministers were given posts: Murong Ping as palace attendant, Huangfu Zhen and Li Hong as court commandants, all with regular attendance at court.

sentences.zh: 李邽為尚書，封衡為尚書郎，慕容德為張掖太守，燕國平睿為宣威將軍，悉羅騰為三署郎。

translations.literal: Li Gui as Master of Writing, Feng Heng as Master of Writing Attendant, Murong De as Zhangye Administrator, Yan Guo Ping Rui as Manifest Might General, Xi Luoteng as Three Offices Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui was made a minister, Feng Heng a secretary, Murong De governor of Zhangye, Ping Rui a general, and Xi Luoteng an officer of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 其餘封授各有差。

translations.literal: The remaining enfeoffments and appointments each had difference.
translations.idiomatic: Others received titles and offices according to rank.

sentences.zh: 衡，裕之子也。

translations.literal: Heng was Yu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Heng was the son of Feng Yu.

sentences.zh: 燕故太史黃泓歎曰：「燕必中興，其在吳王乎！

translations.literal: Yan's former Grand Astrologer Huang Hong sighed: "Yan will surely have central revival—perhaps in the Prince of Wu!
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hong, Yan's former court astrologer, sighed: "Yan will rise again—and the Prince of Wu will be the man!

sentences.zh: 恨吾老，不及見耳！」

translations.literal: I regret I am old—cannot reach to see it!"
translations.idiomatic: Alas that I am too old to live to see it!"

sentences.zh: 汲郡趙秋曰：「天道在燕，而秦滅之。

translations.literal: Zhao Qiu of Ji Commandery said, "Heaven's way was with Yan, yet Qin destroyed it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qiu of Ji Commandery said, "Heaven favored Yan, yet Qin destroyed it.

sentences.zh: 不及十五年，秦必復為燕有。」

translations.literal: Within less than fifteen years Qin will again become Yan's possession."
translations.idiomatic: Within fifteen years Qin will again belong to Yan."

sentences.zh: 慕容桓之子鳳，年十一，陰有復仇之志。

translations.literal: Murong Huan's son Feng, eleven years old, secretly harbored the will to avenge his father.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huan's son Feng, only eleven, secretly nursed a wish for revenge.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑、丁零有氣干者，皆傾身與之交結。

translations.literal: Xianbei and Dingling men of spirit all devoted themselves to befriending him.
translations.idiomatic: Bold Xianbei and Dingling youths all sought his friendship.

sentences.zh: 權翼見而謂之曰：「兒方以才望自顯，勿效爾父不識天命！」

translations.literal: Quan Yi saw this and said to him, "The boy is just making a name by talent and reputation—do not imitate your father in failing to know Heaven's mandate!"
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi saw this and warned him, "You are building a name on talent—do not follow your father in defying Heaven's mandate!"

sentences.zh: 鳳厲色曰：「先王欲建忠而不遂，此乃人臣之節；

translations.literal: Feng said sternly, "The former king wished to establish loyalty but could not complete it—this is a minister's proper duty;
translations.idiomatic: Feng said coldly, "My father wished to serve loyally and could not finish—that is a subject's duty;

sentences.zh: 君侯之言，豈獎勸將來之義乎！」

translations.literal: are my lord's words the sort that encourage what is to come!"
translations.idiomatic: are your words meant to encourage a future worth having!"

sentences.zh: 翼改容謝之，言於秦王堅曰：「慕容鳳忼慨有才器，但狼子野心，恐終不為人用耳。」

translations.literal: Yi changed expression and apologized, then told King of Qin Fu Jian: "Murong Feng is ardent and talented, but he has the heart of a wolf cub—I fear in the end he will not serve others."
translations.idiomatic: Yi apologized and told King Fu Jian, "Murong Feng is bold and able, but he has the heart of a wolf cub and may never truly serve anyone."

sentences.zh: 秦省雍州。

translations.literal: Qin reduced and abolished Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Qin abolished Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 是歲，仇池公楊世卒，子纂立，始與秦絕。

translations.literal: That year Duke of Chouchi Yang Shi died; his son Zuan succeeded and for the first time broke with Qin.
translations.idiomatic: That year Duke of Chouchi Yang Shi died; his son Zuan succeeded and broke with Qin for the first time.

sentences.zh: 叔父武都太守統與之爭國，起兵相攻。

translations.literal: His uncle Tong, administrator of Wudu, disputed the state with him and raised troops to attack each other.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Tong, administrator of Wudu, contested the succession and raised troops against him.
